columns.comment: Dictionary UUID.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Dictionary status. Possible values: NOT_LOADED — Dictionary not currently loaded in memory, LOADED — Dictionary loaded successfully, FAILED — Unable to load the dictionary as a result of an error, LOADING — Dictionary is loading now, LOADED_AND_RELOADING — Dictionary is loaded successfully, and is being reloaded right now (frequent reasons: SYSTEM RELOAD DICTIONARY query, timeout, dictionary co…

columns.name: is_lazy
columns.comment: Whether the dictionary is loaded on first use rather than eagerly. Reflects the `dictionary_lazy_load` setting of the dictionary, or the `dictionaries_lazy_load` server setting if it is `auto`. A lazy dictionary stays in the NOT_LOADED status until it is used for the first time.

columns.name: origin
columns.comment: Path to the configuration file that describes the dictionary.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Type of a dictionary allocation. Storing Dictionaries in Memory.

columns.name: key.names
columns.comment: Array of key names provided by the dictionary.

columns.name: key.types
columns.comment: Corresponding array of key types provided by the dictionary.

columns.name: attribute.names
columns.comment: Array of attribute names provided by the dictionary.

columns.name: attribute.types
columns.comment: Corresponding array of attribute types provided by the dictionary.

columns.name: bytes_allocated
columns.comment: Amount of RAM allocated for the dictionary.

columns.name: hierarchical_index_bytes_allocated
columns.comment: Amount of RAM allocated for hierarchical index.

columns.name: query_count
columns.comment: Number of queries since the dictionary was loaded or since the last successful reboot.

columns.name: hit_rate
columns.comment: For cache dictionaries, the percentage of uses for which the value was in the cache.

columns.name: found_rate
columns.comment: The percentage of uses for which the value was found.

columns.name: element_count
columns.comment: Number of items stored in the dictionary.

columns.name: load_factor
columns.comment: Percentage filled in the dictionary (for a hashed dictionary, the percentage filled in the hash table).

columns.name: source
columns.comment: Text describing the data source for the dictionary.

columns.name: lifetime_min
columns.comment: Minimum lifetime of the dictionary in memory, after which ClickHouse tries to reload the dictionary (if invalidate_query is set, then only if it has changed). Set in seconds.

columns.name: lifetime_max
columns.comment: Maximum lifetime of the dictionary in memory, after which ClickHouse tries to reload the dictionary (if invalidate_query is set, then only if it has changed). Set in seconds.

columns.name: loading_start_time
columns.comment: Start time for loading the dictionary.

columns.name: last_successful_update_time
columns.comment: End time for loading or updating the dictionary. Helps to monitor some troubles with dictionary sources and investigate the causes.

columns.name: error_count
columns.comment: Number of errors since last successful loading. Helps to monitor some troubles with dictionary sources and investigate the causes.

columns.name: loading_duration
columns.comment: Duration of a dictionary loading.

columns.name: last_exception
columns.comment: Text of the error that occurs when creating or reloading the dictionary if the dictionary couldn't be created.

columns.name: comment
columns.comment: Text of the comment to dictionary.

name: dictionary_layouts
comment: .description Contains the list of dictionary layouts supported by the server, along with embedded documentation for each layout. A dictionary layout determines how a dictionary is stored in memory (or on disk) and how it is looked up; it is specified in the `LAYOUT` clause of a `CREATE DICTIONARY` query.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The name of the dictionary layout, as specified in the LAYOUT clause.

columns.name: is_complex
columns.comment: Whether the layout requires a complex key (a key consisting of several attributes or of a non-integer type).

columns.name: description
columns.comment: A description of what the dictionary layout does. For layouts that have a dedicated documentation page, this contains the full Markdown body of that page; for the remaining layouts it is a concise summary.

columns.name: syntax
columns.comment: How the layout is specified in the LAYOUT clause of a CREATE DICTIONARY query.

columns.name: examples
columns.comment: Usage examples.

columns.name: introduced_in
columns.comment: The ClickHouse version in which the layout was first introduced, in the form major.minor.

columns.name: related
columns.comment: The names of related dictionary layouts.

name: dictionary_sources
comment: .description Contains the list of dictionary sources supported by the server, along with embedded documentation for each source. A dictionary source determines where the dictionary data is loaded from; it is specified in the `SOURCE` clause of a `CREATE DICTIONARY` query.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The name of the dictionary source, as specified in the SOURCE clause.

columns.name: description
columns.comment: A description of what the dictionary source does. For sources that have a dedicated documentation page, this contains the full Markdown body of that page; for the remaining sources it is a concise summary.

columns.name: syntax
columns.comment: The structure of the SOURCE clause used to specify the source. Note that some sources are subject to access control when a dictionary is created from a DDL query (as opposed to a server configuration file); see the `description` of the individual source for details.

columns.name: examples
columns.comment: Usage examples.

columns.name: introduced_in
columns.comment: The ClickHouse version in which the source was first introduced, in the form major.minor.

columns.name: related
columns.comment: The names of related dictionary sources.

name: dimensional_metrics
comment: .description This table contains dimensional metrics that can be calculated instantly and exported in the Prometheus format. It is always up to date.

columns.name: metric
columns.comment: Metric name.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: Metric value.

columns.name: description
columns.comment: Metric description.

columns.name: labels
columns.comment: Metric labels.

name: disk_types
comment: .description Contains the list of disk types supported by the server, along with embedded documentation for each type. A disk type is specified in the `type` of a disk configuration and determines where and how a disk stores its data (local filesystem, object storage, a cache over another disk, and so on).

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The name of the disk type, as specified in the `type` of a disk configuration.

columns.name: description
columns.comment: A high-level description of what the disk type does.

columns.name: syntax
columns.comment: How the disk type is specified in a disk configuration.

columns.name: examples
columns.comment: Usage examples.

columns.name: introduced_in
columns.comment: The ClickHouse version in which the disk type was first introduced, in the form major.minor.

columns.name: related
columns.comment: The names of related disk types.

name: disks
comment: .description Contains information about disks defined in the server configuration.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of a disk in the server configuration.

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Path to the mount point in the file system.

columns.name: free_space
columns.comment: Free space on disk in bytes.

columns.name: total_space
columns.comment: Disk volume in bytes.

columns.name: unreserved_space
columns.comment: Free space which is not taken by reservations (free_space minus the size of reservations taken by merges, inserts, and other disk write operations currently running).

columns.name: keep_free_space
columns.comment: Amount of disk space that should stay free on disk in bytes. Defined in the keep_free_space_bytes parameter of disk configuration.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: The disk type which tells where this disk stores the data - RAM, local drive or remote storage.

columns.name: object_storage_type
columns.comment: Type of object storage if disk type is object_storage

columns.name: metadata_type
columns.comment: Type of metadata storage if disk type is object_storage

columns.name: is_encrypted
columns.comment: Flag which shows whether this disk encrypts the underlying data.

columns.name: is_read_only
columns.comment: Flag which indicates that you can only perform read operations with this disk.

columns.name: is_write_once
columns.comment: Flag which indicates if disk is write-once. Which means that it does support BACKUP to this disk, but does not support INSERT into MergeTree table on this disk.

columns.name: is_remote
columns.comment: Flag which indicated what operations with this disk involve network interaction.

columns.name: is_broken
columns.comment: Flag which indicates if disk is broken. Broken disks will have 0 space and cannot be used.

columns.name: cache_path
columns.comment: The path to the cache directory on local drive in case when the disk supports caching.

name: distributed_ddl_queue
comment: .description Contains information about distributed ddl queries (ON CLUSTER clause) that were executed on a cluster.

columns.name: entry
columns.comment: Query id.

columns.name: entry_version
columns.comment: Version of the entry.

columns.name: initiator_host
columns.comment: Host that initiated the DDL operation.

columns.name: initiator_port
columns.comment: Port used by the initiator.

columns.name: cluster
columns.comment: Cluster name, empty if not determined.

columns.name: query
columns.comment: Query executed.

columns.name: settings
columns.comment: Settings used in the DDL operation.

columns.name: query_create_time
columns.comment: Query created time.

columns.name: host
columns.comment: Hostname.

columns.name: port
columns.comment: Host Port.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Status of the query.

columns.name: exception_code
columns.comment: Exception code.

columns.name: exception_text
columns.comment: Exception message.

columns.name: query_finish_time
columns.comment: Query finish time.

columns.name: query_duration_ms
columns.comment: Duration of query execution (in milliseconds).

name: distribution_queue
comment: .description Contains information about local files that are in the queue to be sent to the shards. These local files contain new parts that are created by inserting new data into the Distributed table in asynchronous mode.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Name of the database.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Name of the table.

columns.name: data_path
columns.comment: Path to the folder with local files.

columns.name: is_blocked
columns.comment: Flag indicates whether sending local files to the server is blocked.

columns.name: error_count
columns.comment: Number of errors.

columns.name: data_files
columns.comment: Number of local files in a folder.

columns.name: data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Size of compressed data in local files, in bytes.

columns.name: broken_data_files
columns.comment: Number of files that has been marked as broken (due to an error).

columns.name: broken_data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Size of compressed data in broken files, in bytes.

columns.name: last_exception
columns.comment: Text message about the last error that occurred (if any).

columns.name: last_exception_time
columns.comment: Time when last exception occurred.

name: dns_cache
comment: .description Contains information about cached DNS records.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname.

columns.name: ip_address
columns.comment: IP address.

columns.name: ip_family
columns.comment: IP address family.

columns.name: cached_at
columns.comment: Record cached timestamp.

name: documentation
comment: .description Collects the embedded documentation of the uniform components of the system into a single table. Every row corresponds to one entity (a function, a table engine, a data type, and so on) and contains its embedded reference documentation rendered as Markdown. This content backs generated website documentation and the per-kind `system.*` tables; website pages may add MDX-only preamble…

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The name of the entity, e.g. `domainWithoutWWW` or `MergeTree`.

columns.name: type
columns.type: Enum8('Function' = 1, 'Aggregate Function' = 2, 'Table Function' = 3, 'Table Engine' = 4, 'Database Engine' = 5, 'Data Type' = 6, 'Dictionary Layout' = 7, 'Dictionary Source' = 8, 'Aggregate Function Combinator' = 9, 'Data Skipping Index' = 10, 'Disk Type' = 11, 'Setting' = 12, 'MergeTree Setting' = 13, 'Server Setting' = 14, 'Format' = 15, 'Compression Codec' = 16, 'Profile Event' = 17, 'Current Metric' = 18, 'Asynchronous Metric' = 19, 'System Table' = 20, 'Statement' = 21)
columns.comment: The kind of the entity, e.g. `Function` or `Table Engine`.

columns.name: description
columns.comment: The reference documentation of the entity rendered as Markdown, assembled from the embedded documentation and including syntax, examples and other structured parts, if any. Website pages may add MDX-only preambles or guidance outside their generated bodies.

columns.name: source
columns.comment: The path to the source file where the entity's documentation is defined, relative to the repository root. Empty if the source location is unknown.

name: dropped_tables
comment: .description Contains information about tables that drop table has been executed on but for which data cleanup has not yet been performed.

columns.name: index
columns.comment: Index in marked_dropped_tables queue.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Database name.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: uuid
columns.comment: Table UUID.

columns.name: engine
columns.comment: Table engine name.

columns.name: metadata_dropped_path
columns.comment: Path of table's metadata file in metadata_dropped directory.

columns.name: table_dropped_time
columns.comment: The time when the next attempt to remove table's data is scheduled on. Usually it's the table when the table was dropped plus `database_atomic_delay_before_drop_table_sec`.

name: dropped_tables_parts
comment: .description Contains information about parts of MergeTree dropped tables from system.dropped_tables

columns.name: partition
columns.comment: Partition identifier (string representation derived from the table partition key expression).

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the data part. The part naming structure can be used to determine many aspects of the data, ingest, and merge patterns. The part naming format is the following:

columns.name: uuid
columns.comment: The UUID of data part.

columns.name: part_type
columns.comment: The data part storing format. Possible values: `Wide` — each column is stored in a separate file, `Compact` — all columns are stored in one file. Data storing format is controlled by the `min_bytes_for_wide_part` and `min_rows_for_wide_part` settings of the MergeTree table.

columns.name: part_storage_type
columns.comment: The type of `DataPartStorage`. Possible values: `Packed` - most part files are stored in a single archive (projections and a few service files such as `txn_version.txt` are written separately), `Full` - each file is stored separately.

columns.name: active
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the data part is active. If a data part is active, it's used in a table. Otherwise, it's about to be deleted. Inactive data parts appear after merging and mutating operations.

columns.name: marks
columns.comment: The number of marks. To get the approximate number of rows in a data part, multiply marks by the index granularity (usually 8192) (this hint does not work for adaptive granularity).

columns.name: rows
columns.comment: The number of rows.

columns.name: files
columns.comment: The number of files in the data part.

columns.name: bytes_on_disk
columns.comment: Total size of all the data part files in bytes.

columns.name: data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of compressed data in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: data_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of uncompressed data in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: primary_key_size
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) used by primary key values in the primary.idx/cidx file on disk.

columns.name: marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of the file with marks.

columns.name: secondary_indices_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of compressed data for secondary indices in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: secondary_indices_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of uncompressed data for secondary indices in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: secondary_indices_marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of the file with marks for secondary indices.

columns.name: modification_time
columns.comment: The time the directory with the data part was modified. This usually corresponds to the time of data part creation.

columns.name: remove_time
columns.comment: The time when the data part became inactive.

columns.name: refcount
columns.comment: The number of places where the data part is used. A value greater than 2 indicates that the data part is used in queries or merges.

columns.name: min_date
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date key in the data part.

columns.name: max_date
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date key in the data part.

columns.name: min_time
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date and time key in the data part.

columns.name: max_time
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date and time key in the data part.

columns.name: partition_id
columns.comment: ID of the partition.

columns.name: min_block_number
columns.comment: The minimum number of data parts that make up the current part after merging.

columns.name: max_block_number
columns.comment: The maximum number of data parts that make up the current part after merging.

columns.name: level
columns.comment: Depth of the merge tree. Zero means that the current part was created by insert rather than by merging other parts.

columns.name: data_version
columns.comment: Number that is used to determine which mutations should be applied to the data part (mutations with a version higher than data_version).

columns.name: primary_key_bytes_in_memory
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) used by primary key values. Will be 0 when `primary_key_lazy_load` is enabled and the key is not loaded. When non-zero the bytes live in the part itself and are accounted within `jemalloc.mergetree_arena.active_bytes`. They are NEVER counted in `PrimaryIndexCacheBytes` — those are mutually exclusive per part: an index lives either in the part (this metric) or in …

columns.name: primary_key_bytes_in_memory_allocated
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) reserved for primary key values. Will be 0 when `primary_key_lazy_load` is enabled and the key is not loaded. When non-zero, included in `jemalloc.mergetree_arena.active_bytes`. See the note on `primary_key_bytes_in_memory` for the relationship with `PrimaryIndexCacheBytes`.

columns.name: index_granularity_bytes_in_memory
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) used by index granularity values (will be 0 in case of primary_key_lazy_load=1 and use_primary_key_cache=1). When non-zero the bytes are part-owned and accounted within `jemalloc.mergetree_arena.active_bytes`.

columns.name: index_granularity_bytes_in_memory_allocated
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) reserved for index granularity values (will be 0 in case of primary_key_lazy_load=1 and use_primary_key_cache=1). When non-zero, included in `jemalloc.mergetree_arena.active_bytes`.

columns.name: is_frozen
columns.comment: Flag that shows that a partition data backup exists. 1, the backup exists. 0, the backup does not exist. For more details, see FREEZE PARTITION.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Name of the database.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Name of the table.

columns.name: engine
columns.comment: Name of the table engine without parameters.

columns.name: disk_name
columns.comment: Name of a disk that stores the data part.

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Absolute path to the folder with data part files.

columns.name: hash_of_all_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of compressed files.

columns.name: hash_of_uncompressed_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of uncompressed files (files with marks, index file etc.).

columns.name: uncompressed_hash_of_compressed_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of data in the compressed files as if they were uncompressed.

columns.name: delete_ttl_info_min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date and time key for TTL DELETE rule.

columns.name: delete_ttl_info_max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date and time key for TTL DELETE rule.

columns.name: move_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: Array of expressions. Each expression defines a TTL MOVE rule.

columns.name: move_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: Array of date and time values. Each element describes the minimum key value for a TTL MOVE rule.

columns.name: move_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: Array of date and time values. Each element describes the maximum key value for a TTL MOVE rule.

columns.name: default_compression_codec
columns.comment: The name of the codec used to compress this data part when a column has no explicit codec or uses `CODEC(Default)`. `UNKNOWN` means this codec could not be recovered exactly from the part metadata. With `enable_adaptive_codec_selection`, individual blocks of such columns may use other codecs; see `mergeTreeCodecBlockCounts`.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: projections
columns.comment: The list of projection names calculated for this part.

columns.name: visible
columns.comment: Flag which indicated whether this part is visible for SELECT queries.

columns.name: creation_tid
columns.comment: ID of transaction that has created/is trying to create this object.

columns.name: removal_tid_lock
columns.comment: Hash of removal_tid, used to lock an object for removal.

columns.name: removal_tid
columns.comment: ID of transaction that has removed/is trying to remove this object

columns.name: creation_csn
columns.comment: CSN of transaction that has created this object

columns.name: removal_csn
columns.comment: CSN of transaction that has removed this object

columns.name: has_lightweight_delete
columns.comment: The flag which indicated whether the part has lightweight delete mask.

columns.name: last_removal_attempt_time
columns.comment: The last time the server tried to delete this part.

columns.name: removal_state
columns.comment: The current state of part removal process.

name: enabled_roles
comment: .description Contains all active roles at the moment, including the current role of the current user and granted roles for the current role.

columns.name: role_name
columns.comment: Role name.

columns.name: with_admin_option
columns.comment: 1 if the role has ADMIN OPTION privilege.

columns.name: is_current
columns.comment: Flag that shows whether `enabled_role` is a current role of a current user.

columns.name: is_default
columns.comment: Flag that shows whether `enabled_role` is a default role.

name: error_log
comment: .description Contains history of error values from table `system.errors`, periodically flushed to disk.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: clickhouse_version
columns.comment: Version of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: system_processor
columns.comment: CPU architecture of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Event date.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Event time.

columns.name: code
columns.comment: Error code.

columns.name: error
columns.comment: Error name.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: Number of errors happened in time interval.

columns.name: remote
columns.comment: Remote exception (i.e. received during one of the distributed queries).

columns.name: last_error_time
columns.comment: The time when the last error happened.

columns.name: last_error_message
columns.comment: Message for the last error.

columns.name: last_error_query_id
columns.comment: Id of a query that caused the last error (if available).

columns.name: last_error_trace
columns.comment: A stack trace of the last error. On ELF platforms except FreeBSD, addresses inside the main ClickHouse binary are stored as physical file offsets, and frames outside it (shared libraries, JIT code) are stored as 0.

columns.name: last_error_symbols
columns.comment: Demangled symbol names corresponding to last_error_trace.

columns.name: last_error_lines
columns.comment: File names with line numbers corresponding to last_error_trace.

name: errors
comment: .description Contains error codes with the number of times they have been triggered.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the error (errorCodeToName).

columns.name: code
columns.comment: Code number of the error.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: The number of times this error happened.

columns.name: last_error_time
columns.comment: The time when the last error happened.

columns.name: last_error_message
columns.comment: Message for the last error.

columns.name: last_error_format_string
columns.comment: Format string for the last error.

columns.name: last_error_trace
columns.comment: A stack trace of the last error. On ELF platforms except FreeBSD, addresses inside the main ClickHouse binary are stored as physical file offsets, and frames outside it (shared libraries, JIT code) are stored as 0.

columns.name: remote
columns.comment: Remote exception (i.e. received during one of the distributed queries).

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: Id of a query that caused an error (if available).

columns.name: last_error_symbols
columns.comment: Demangled symbol names corresponding to last_error_trace.

columns.name: last_error_lines
columns.comment: File names with line numbers corresponding to last_error_trace.

name: events
comment: .description Contains information about the number of events that have occurred in the system. For example, in the table, you can find how many `SELECT` queries were processed since the ClickHouse server started.

columns.name: event
columns.comment: Event name.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: Number of events occurred.

columns.name: description
columns.comment: Event description.

name: fail_points
comment: .description Contains a list of all available failpoints registered in the server, along with their type and whether they are currently enabled.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the failpoint.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Type of failpoint: 'once' fires a single time then auto-disables, 'regular' fires every time, 'pauseable_once' blocks execution once, 'pauseable' blocks execution every time until resumed.

columns.name: enabled
columns.comment: Whether the failpoint is currently enabled (1) or disabled (0).

name: filesystem_cache
comment: .description Contains information about all entries inside filesystem cache for remote objects.

columns.name: cache_name
columns.comment: Name of the cache object. Can be used in `SYSTEM DESCRIBE FILESYSTEM CACHE <name>`, `SYSTEM DROP FILESYSTEM CACHE <name>` commands

columns.name: cache_base_path
columns.comment: Path to the base directory where all cache files (of a cache identified by `cache_name`) are stored.

columns.name: cache_path
columns.comment: Path to a particular cache file, corresponding to a file segment in a source file

columns.name: key
columns.comment: Cache key of the file segment

columns.name: file_segment_range_begin
columns.comment: Offset corresponding to the beginning of the file segment range

columns.name: file_segment_range_end
columns.comment: Offset corresponding to the (including) end of the file segment range

columns.name: size
columns.comment: Size of the file segment: the logical size of its range. It is not affected by the `use_real_disk_size` cache setting, which only changes how reservations are accounted in the cache size metrics. Use `downloaded_size` for the number of bytes actually written for this segment

columns.name: state
columns.comment: File segment state (DOWNLOADED, DOWNLOADING, PARTIALLY_DOWNLOADED, ...)

columns.name: finished_download_time
columns.comment: Time when file segment finished downloading.

columns.name: cache_hits
columns.comment: Number of cache hits of corresponding file segment

columns.name: references
columns.comment: Number of references to corresponding file segment. Value 1 means that nobody uses it at the moment (the only existing reference is in cache storage itself)

columns.name: downloaded_size
columns.comment: Downloaded size of the file segment

columns.name: kind
columns.comment: File segment kind (used to distinguish between file segments added as a part of 'Temporary data in cache')

columns.name: unbound
columns.comment: Internal implementation flag

columns.name: user_id
columns.comment: User id of the user which created the file segment

columns.name: segment_type
columns.comment: Type of the segment. Used to separate data files(`.json`, `.txt` and etc) from data file(`.bin`, mark files).

columns.name: file_size
columns.comment: File size of the file to which current file segment belongs

name: filesystem_cache_settings
comment: .description Contains information about all filesystem cache settings

columns.name: cache_name
columns.comment: Cache name

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Cache directory path

columns.name: max_size
columns.comment: Maximum cache size

columns.name: max_elements
columns.comment: Maximum number of cache elements, e.g. file segments (limits number of files on filesystem)

columns.name: max_file_segment_size
columns.comment: Maximum size of a single file segment

columns.name: boundary_alignment
columns.comment: File segment alignment

columns.name: reserve_granularity
columns.comment: Maximum size to reserve ahead of the downloaded size of a file segment, to take the cache lock less often. Starts from 0 for each reader/writer and grows with its repeated reservations up to this value. 0 disables reserve-ahead.

columns.name: cache_on_write_operations
columns.comment: Enables write-through cache (cache on INSERT and MERGE)

columns.name: cache_policy
columns.comment: Cache eviction policy

columns.name: slru_size_ratio
columns.comment: SLRU cache policy size ratio of protected to probationary elements

columns.name: background_download_threads
columns.comment: Number of background download threads. Value 0 disables background download

columns.name: background_download_queue_size_limit
columns.comment: Maximum number of file segments in the background download queue. Value 0 means no limit. Background download is disabled when background_download_threads is 0

columns.name: background_download_max_file_segment_size
columns.comment: Alignment-rounded prefetch threshold for an already-started segment, not a cap on total segment size. Below this size, background download fills up to the value rounded up to boundary_alignment. Once downloaded_size reaches it, background download continues up to downloaded_size rounded up to boundary_alignment

columns.name: load_metadata_threads
columns.comment: Maximum number of threads used to load cache metadata at server startup

columns.name: load_metadata_asynchronously
columns.comment: Enables asynchronous loading of metadata on server startup

columns.name: keep_free_space_size_ratio
columns.comment: A ratio of free space which cache would try to uphold in the background

columns.name: keep_free_space_elements_ratio
columns.comment: A ratio of free elements which cache would try to uphold in the background

columns.name: keep_free_space_remove_batch
columns.comment: A remove batch size of cache elements made by background thread which upholds free space/elements ratio

columns.name: keep_free_space_eviction_threads
columns.comment: Number of threads which perform the actual file segment removal (filesystem deletion) for the background free space/elements ratio keeping. The single background thread collects eviction candidates and frees their priority queue entries, while these threads do the lock-free removal in parallel

columns.name: invalidated_entries_cleanup_interval_ms
columns.comment: Idle interval in milliseconds of the background task which purges invalidated (lazily-removed) priority queue entries

columns.name: invalidated_entries_cleanup_threshold
columns.comment: Number of accumulated invalidated priority queue entries which triggers their background removal

columns.name: invalidated_entries_cleanup_remove_batch
columns.comment: Maximum number of invalidated priority queue entries removed under a single write lock per background iteration

columns.name: enable_filesystem_query_cache_limit
columns.comment: Enable limiting maximum size of cache which can be written within a query

columns.name: cache_hits_threshold
columns.comment: Deprecated setting

columns.name: enable_bypass_cache_with_threshold
columns.comment: Undocumented. Not recommended for use

columns.name: bypass_cache_threshold
columns.comment: Undocumented. Not recommended for use

columns.name: write_cache_per_user_id_directory
columns.comment: Deprecated setting, ignored. The behavior is now determined automatically based on cache policy

columns.name: allow_dynamic_cache_resize
columns.comment: Allow dynamic resize of filesystem cache

columns.name: dynamic_resize_lock_wait_ms
columns.comment: Timeout in milliseconds to acquire the dynamic resize exclusive lock before skipping the resize attempt

columns.name: max_size_ratio_to_total_space
columns.comment: Ratio of `max_size` to total disk space

columns.name: skip_cache_on_disk_failure
columns.comment: If true, bypass filesystem cache operations silently on disk IO errors. If false (default), disk IO errors are propagated as startup failures.

columns.name: use_split_cache
columns.comment: Use separation of files to system/data.

columns.name: split_cache_ratio
columns.comment: Ratio of system segment to total size of cache for split_cache.

columns.name: system_cache_extensions
columns.comment: Comma-separated list of file extensions that are classified as system cache segments when `use_split_cache` is enabled. When changed, existing cache entries remain in their previous segment type and are evicted naturally over time. Restart is required to change this setting.

columns.name: overcommit_eviction_evict_step
columns.comment: Eviction step in bytes for overcommit eviction policy. Used for keep_free_space_*_ratio settings

columns.name: check_cache_probability
columns.comment: Works only for debug or sanitizer build. Checks cache correctness by going through all cache and checking state of each cache element

columns.name: idle_client_ttl_sec
columns.comment: If non-zero and the cache policy tracks per-client usage, all cache entries that belong to a client (user_id) which has not been accessed for this many seconds are fully removed from the cache. Each access by the client refreshes the timer. Default is 1 week. Used by the distributed cache server.

columns.name: idle_client_check_interval_sec
columns.comment: How often the idle client eviction task runs, in seconds. Only meaningful when `idle_client_ttl_sec` is non-zero. 0 means an automatic value (`max(1, idle_client_ttl_sec / 10)`).

columns.name: client_weight_persist_interval_sec
columns.comment: How often the per-client weights are written to disk, in seconds, so that a client which has not reconnected yet keeps its weight across a restart. The first write happens one interval after startup, and a clean shutdown writes them out as well. Only meaningful when the cache policy tracks per-client usage.

columns.name: idle_client_eviction_threads
columns.comment: Maximum number of threads used to purge idle clients' cache. Only meaningful when `idle_client_ttl_sec` is non-zero.

columns.name: expose_prometheus_eviction_metrics
columns.comment: Expose Prometheus metrics for filesystem cache eviction activity (`filesystem_cache_evictions_total` etc.). Off by default. Can be toggled at runtime via `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG`.

columns.name: expose_prometheus_eviction_metrics_per_user
columns.comment: Additionally expose per-user-id eviction metrics. Requires `expose_prometheus_eviction_metrics`. Cardinality grows with distinct evicting users.

columns.name: use_real_disk_size
columns.comment: Account cached file reservations of this cache in filesystem block-aligned units (an approximation of the physical on-disk size, not the exact allocated size) instead of reserved bytes. This affects `current_size` of this cache. The process-wide `FilesystemCacheSize` metric and the eviction-size profile events sum over all caches, so they uniformly reflect the reservation footprint only when al…

columns.name: drop_cache_threads
columns.comment: Maximum number of threads used to remove cache keys in parallel on `SYSTEM DROP FILESYSTEM CACHE`. Value 1 means the removal is performed by the query thread alone

columns.name: is_initialized
columns.comment: Indicates whether cache was successfully initialized

columns.name: current_size
columns.comment: Current cache size: the space currently charged to or held by the cache priority queue. It consists of the reserved sizes of the cache file segments plus the space temporarily held while a reservation or an eviction is in progress, so it can momentarily exceed the sum over the file segments in `system.filesystem_cache`. If `use_real_disk_size` is enabled for this cache, the reservations are acc…

columns.name: current_elements_num
columns.comment: Current cache elements (file segments) number

name: jemalloc_arena_bins
comment: .description Same as `system.jemalloc_bins` but with one row per (arena, bin) instead of aggregating over arenas. Slabs belong to a single arena, so this table locates fragmentation in a specific arena (including the dedicated `MergeTree` metadata, JIT and cache arenas) and joins to `system.jemalloc_sampled_allocations` on both `arena` and size class.

columns.comment: Index of the arena. Joins to `system.jemalloc_sampled_allocations.arena`.

columns.name: purpose
columns.comment: Purpose of a dedicated long-lived arena: 'mergetree' (part and table metadata), 'jit', 'cache'. Empty for general-purpose arenas. Dedicated arenas hold long-lived allocations by design; fragmentation reports usually exclude them.

columns.name: index
columns.comment: Index of the bin ordered by size.

columns.name: large
columns.comment: True for large allocations and False for small.

columns.name: size
columns.comment: Size of allocations in this bin.

columns.name: allocations
columns.comment: Number of allocations.

columns.name: deallocations
columns.comment: Number of deallocations.

columns.name: nregs
columns.comment: Number of regions per slab.

columns.name: curslabs
columns.comment: Current number of slabs.

columns.name: curregs
columns.comment: Current number of regions for this size class.

columns.name: slab_size
columns.comment: Size of each slab in bytes. Zero for large size classes, which are not slab-based.

columns.name: nonfull_slabs
columns.comment: Current number of slabs that contain at least one free region. Zero for large size classes.

name: jemalloc_bins
comment: .description Contains information about memory allocations done via jemalloc allocator in different size classes (bins) aggregated from all arenas. These statistics might not be absolutely accurate because of thread local caching in jemalloc.

columns.name: index
columns.comment: Index of the bin ordered by size.

columns.name: large

columns.name: size
columns.comment: Size of allocations in this bin.

columns.name: allocations

columns.name: deallocations
columns.comment: Number of deallocations.

columns.name: nregs

columns.name: curslabs
columns.comment: Current number of slabs.

columns.name: curregs
columns.comment: Current number of regions for this size class.

columns.name: slab_size
columns.comment: Size of each slab in bytes. Zero for large size classes, which are not slab-based.

columns.name: nonfull_slabs

name: jemalloc_profile_text
comment: .description Displays the symbolized jemalloc heap profile. Run 'SYSTEM JEMALLOC FLUSH PROFILE' to generate a profile first.

columns.name: line
columns.comment: Line from the symbolized jemalloc heap profile.

name: jemalloc_sampled_allocations
comment: .description One row per live sampled allocation from the jemalloc heap profiler; reading the table flushes a fresh heap profile. Only threads with the profiler armed contribute (`jemalloc_enable_profiler` setting or `jemalloc_enable_global_profiler` config); each row represents roughly `weight` similar allocations.

columns.name: trace
columns.comment: Addresses of the allocating backtrace, leaf frame first. Addresses inside the main ClickHouse binary are stored as offsets in it (same convention as `system.trace_log.trace`), and frames outside it are stored as 0. Empty if jemalloc could not unwind the stack. Symbolize with `addressToSymbol` and `demangle` (requires `allow_introspection_functions`).

columns.name: age_ns
columns.comment: Time in nanoseconds the allocation has been alive, relative to the moment the profile was flushed.

columns.name: size
columns.comment: Requested allocation size in bytes.

columns.name: usize
columns.comment: Usable size in bytes, i.e. the size class the request was rounded up to.

columns.name: size_class
columns.comment: Index of the size class. Joins to `system.jemalloc_bins.index` for small size classes.

columns.name: arena
columns.comment: Index of the arena the allocation was served from.

columns.name: thr_uid
columns.comment: jemalloc-internal unique id of the allocating thread.

columns.name: sample_interval
columns.comment: Average number of allocated bytes between samples, taken from the profile header. The same for all rows.

name: jemalloc_stats
comment: .description Returns jemalloc statistics in a single row with a single column. Equivalent to SYSTEM JEMALLOC STATS command.

columns.name: stats
columns.comment: JEMalloc statistics output from malloc_stats_print.

columns.name: histograms.count
