columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: projections
columns.comment: The list of projection names calculated for this part.

columns.name: visible
columns.comment: Flag which indicated whether this part is visible for SELECT queries.

columns.name: creation_tid
columns.comment: ID of transaction that has created/is trying to create this object.

columns.name: removal_tid_lock
columns.comment: Hash of removal_tid, used to lock an object for removal.

columns.name: removal_tid
columns.comment: ID of transaction that has removed/is trying to remove this object

columns.name: creation_csn
columns.comment: CSN of transaction that has created this object

columns.comment: CSN of transaction that has removed this object

columns.name: has_lightweight_delete

columns.name: last_removal_attempt_time
columns.comment: The last time the server tried to delete this part.

columns.name: removal_state
columns.comment: The current state of part removal process.

name: processes
comment: .description This system table is used for implementing the `SHOW PROCESSLIST` query.

columns.name: is_initial_query
columns.comment: Whether the query is initial. Possible values: 1 — an initial (top-level) query, 0 — a child query initiated by another query, including queries for distributed execution and internal subqueries.

columns.name: user
columns.comment: The user who made the query. Keep in mind that for distributed processing, queries are sent to remote servers under the default user. The field contains the username for a specific query, not for a query that this query initiated.

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: Query ID, if defined.

columns.name: address
columns.comment: The IP address the query was made from. The same for distributed processing. To track where a distributed query was originally made from, look at system.processes on the query requestor server.

columns.name: port
columns.comment: The client port the query was made from.

columns.name: initial_user
columns.comment: Name of the user who ran the initial query in the same query chain.

columns.name: initial_query_id
columns.comment: ID of the initial query in the same query chain.

columns.name: initial_address
columns.comment: IP address from which the initial query in the same query chain was launched.

columns.name: initial_port
columns.comment: Client port from which the initial query in the same query chain was launched.

columns.name: interface
columns.comment: The interface which was used to send the query, as reported by the client. `Unknown` if the reported interface is not one this server recognizes.

columns.name: os_user
columns.comment: Operating system username who runs clickhouse-client.

columns.name: client_hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the client machine where the clickhouse-client or another TCP client is run.

columns.name: client_name
columns.comment: The clickhouse-client or another TCP client name.

columns.name: client_agent
columns.comment: The AI coding agent that invoked the client (e.g. `claude-code`, `cursor`), detected from environment variables. Empty if no agent was detected.

columns.name: client_revision
columns.comment: Revision of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.name: client_version_major
columns.comment: Major version of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.name: client_version_minor
columns.comment: Minor version of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.name: client_version_patch
columns.comment: Patch component of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client version.

columns.name: http_method
columns.comment: HTTP method that initiated the query. `UNKNOWN` if the query did not arrive over HTTP, or if the reported method is not one this server recognizes.

columns.name: http_user_agent
columns.comment: HTTP header UserAgent passed in the HTTP query.

columns.name: http_referer
columns.comment: HTTP header Referer passed in the HTTP query (contains an absolute or partial address of the page making the query).

columns.name: forwarded_for
columns.comment: HTTP header X-Forwarded-For passed in the HTTP query.

columns.name: quota_key
columns.comment: The quota key specified in the quotas setting (see keyed).

columns.name: distributed_depth
columns.comment: The number of times query was retransmitted between server nodes internally.

columns.name: elapsed
columns.comment: The time in seconds since request execution started.

columns.name: is_cancelled
columns.comment: Was query cancelled.

columns.name: is_all_data_sent
columns.comment: Was all data sent to the client (in other words query had been finished on the server).

columns.name: read_rows
columns.comment: The number of rows read from the table. For distributed processing, on the requestor server, this is the total for all remote servers.

columns.name: read_bytes
columns.comment: The number of uncompressed bytes read from the table. For distributed processing, on the requestor server, this is the total for all remote servers.

columns.name: total_rows_approx
columns.comment: The approximation of the total number of rows that should be read. For distributed processing, on the requestor server, this is the total for all remote servers. It can be updated during request processing, when new sources to process become known.

columns.name: written_rows
columns.comment: The amount of rows written to the storage.

columns.name: written_bytes
columns.comment: The amount of bytes written to the storage.

columns.name: memory_usage
columns.comment: Amount of RAM the query uses. It might not include some types of dedicated memory

columns.name: peak_memory_usage
columns.comment: The current peak of memory usage.

columns.name: spillable_memory_bytes
columns.comment: The current spillable memory.

columns.name: query
columns.comment: The query text. For INSERT, it does not include the data to insert.

columns.name: normalized_query_hash
columns.comment: A numeric hash value, such as it is identical for queries differ only by values of literals.

columns.name: query_kind
columns.comment: The type of the query - SELECT, INSERT, etc.

columns.name: thread_ids
columns.comment: The list of identifiers of all threads which participated in this query.

columns.name: peak_threads_usage
columns.comment: Maximum count of simultaneous threads executing the query.

columns.name: ProfileEvents
columns.comment: ProfileEvents calculated for this query.

columns.name: Settings
columns.comment: The list of modified user-level settings.

columns.name: current_database
columns.comment: The name of the current database.

columns.name: is_internal
columns.comment: Indicates whether it is an auxiliary query executed internally.

name: processors_profile_log
comment: .description This table contains profiling on processors level (that you can find in `EXPLAIN PIPELINE`).

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: clickhouse_version
columns.comment: Version of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: system_processor
columns.comment: CPU architecture of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: The date when the event happened.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: The date and time when the event happened.

columns.name: event_time_microseconds
columns.comment: The date and time with microseconds precision when the event happened.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: ID of processor, unique within the query. It is the number in `processor_uniq_id`.

columns.name: parent_ids
columns.comment: Parent processors IDs.

columns.name: plan_step
columns.comment: ID of the query plan step which created this processor, unique within the query. It is one plus the number in `step_uniq_id`. The value is zero if the processor was not added from any step.

columns.name: plan_step_name
columns.comment: Name of the query plan step which created this processor. The value is empty if the processor was not added from any step.

columns.name: plan_step_description
columns.comment: Description of the query plan step which created this processor. The value is empty if the processor was not added from any step.

columns.name: plan_group
columns.comment: Group of the processor if it was created by query plan step. A group is a logical partitioning of processors added from the same query plan step. Group is used only for beautifying the result of EXPLAIN PIPELINE result.

columns.name: initial_query_id
columns.comment: ID of the initial query in the same query chain.

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: ID of the query.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the processor.

columns.name: elapsed_us
columns.comment: Number of microseconds this processor was executed.

columns.name: input_wait_elapsed_us
columns.comment: Number of microseconds this processor was waiting for data (from other processor).

columns.name: output_wait_elapsed_us
columns.comment: Number of microseconds this processor was waiting because output port was full.

columns.name: input_rows
columns.comment: The number of rows consumed by processor.

columns.name: input_bytes
columns.comment: The number of bytes consumed by processor.

columns.name: output_rows
columns.comment: The number of rows generated by processor.

columns.name: output_bytes
columns.comment: The number of bytes generated by processor.

columns.name: processor_uniq_id
columns.comment: The uniq processor id in pipeline.

columns.name: step_uniq_id
columns.comment: The uniq step id in plan.

columns.name: exception_code
columns.comment: Code of the exception if the query failed, otherwise 0.

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Message of the exception if the query failed, otherwise empty.

name: projection_parts
comment: .description This table contains information about projection parts for tables of the MergeTree family.

columns.name: partition
columns.comment: The partition name.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the data part.

columns.name: part_type
columns.comment: The data part storing format. Possible Values: Wide (a file per column) and Compact (a single file for all columns).

columns.name: parent_name
columns.comment: The name of the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: parent_uuid
columns.comment: The UUID of the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: parent_part_type
columns.comment: The source (parent) data part storing format.

columns.name: active
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the data part is active. If a data part is active, it's used in a table. Otherwise, it's about to be deleted. Inactive data parts appear after merging and mutating operations.

columns.name: marks
columns.comment: The number of marks. To get the approximate number of rows in a data part, multiply marks by the index granularity (usually 8192) (this hint does not work for adaptive granularity).

columns.name: rows
columns.comment: The number of rows.

columns.name: files
columns.comment: The number of files in the data part.

columns.name: bytes_on_disk
columns.comment: Total size of all the data part files in bytes.

columns.name: data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of compressed data in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: data_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of uncompressed data in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of the file with marks.

columns.name: parent_marks
columns.comment: The number of marks in the source (parent) part.

columns.name: parent_rows
columns.comment: The number of rows in the source (parent) part.

columns.name: parent_bytes_on_disk
columns.comment: Total size of all the source (parent) data part files in bytes.

columns.name: parent_data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of compressed data in the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: parent_data_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of uncompressed data in the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: parent_marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of the file with marks in the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: modification_time
columns.comment: The time the directory with the data part was modified. This usually corresponds to the time of data part creation.

columns.name: remove_time
columns.comment: The time when the data part became inactive.

columns.name: refcount
columns.comment: The number of places where the data part is used. A value greater than 2 indicates that the data part is used in queries or merges.

columns.name: min_date
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date key in the data part.

columns.name: max_date
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date key in the data part.

columns.name: min_time
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date and time key in the data part.

columns.name: max_time
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date and time key in the data part.

columns.name: partition_id
columns.comment: ID of the partition.

columns.name: min_block_number
columns.comment: The minimum number of data parts that make up the current part after merging.

columns.name: max_block_number
columns.comment: The maximum number of data parts that make up the current part after merging.

columns.name: level
columns.comment: Depth of the merge tree. Zero means that the current part was created by insert rather than by merging other parts.

columns.name: data_version
columns.comment: Number that is used to determine which mutations should be applied to the data part (mutations with a version higher than data_version).

columns.name: primary_key_bytes_in_memory
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) used by primary key values.

columns.name: primary_key_bytes_in_memory_allocated
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) reserved for primary key values.

columns.name: is_frozen
columns.comment: Flag that shows that a partition data backup exists. 1, the backup exists. 0, the backup does not exist.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Name of the database.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Name of the table.

columns.name: engine
columns.comment: Name of the table engine without parameters.

columns.name: disk_name
columns.comment: Name of a disk that stores the data part.

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Absolute path to the folder with data part files.

columns.name: hash_of_all_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of compressed files.

columns.name: hash_of_uncompressed_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of uncompressed files (files with marks, index file etc.).

columns.name: uncompressed_hash_of_compressed_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of data in the compressed files as if they were uncompressed.

columns.name: delete_ttl_info_min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date and time key for TTL DELETE rule.

columns.name: delete_ttl_info_max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date and time key for TTL DELETE rule.

columns.name: move_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: Array of expressions. Each expression defines a TTL MOVE rule.

columns.name: move_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: Array of date and time values. Each element describes the minimum key value for a TTL MOVE rule.

columns.name: move_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: Array of date and time values. Each element describes the maximum key value for a TTL MOVE rule.

columns.name: default_compression_codec
columns.comment: The name of the codec used to compress this data part (in case when there is no explicit codec for columns). `UNKNOWN` means this codec could not be recovered exactly from the part metadata.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: is_broken
columns.comment: Whether projection part is broken

columns.name: exception_code
columns.comment: Exception message explaining broken state of the projection part

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Exception code explaining broken state of the projection part

columns.name: column_data_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of the decompressed data in the column, in bytes.

columns.name: column_marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of the column with marks, in bytes.

columns.name: column_modification_time
columns.comment: The last time the column was modified.

name: projections

columns.name: database

columns.name: table

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Projection name.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Projection type.

columns.name: sorting_key

columns.name: query

name: query_cache

columns.name: query

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: ID of the query.

columns.name: is_subquery
columns.comment: Whether the query cache entry is a subquery result.

columns.name: result_size
columns.comment: Size of the query cache entry.

columns.name: tag
columns.comment: Tag of the query cache entry.

columns.name: stale
columns.comment: If the query cache entry is stale.

columns.name: shared
columns.comment: If the query cache entry is shared between multiple users.

columns.name: compressed
columns.comment: If the query cache entry is compressed.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.comment: When the query cache entry becomes stale.

columns.name: key_hash
columns.comment: A hash of the query string, used as a key to find query cache entries.

name: query_condition_cache
comment: .description Shows the content of the query condition cache.

columns.name: key_hash
columns.comment: Hash of (table_uuid, part_name, condition_hash).

columns.name: entry_size
columns.comment: The size of the entry in bytes.

columns.name: matching_marks
columns.comment: Matching marks.

name: query_log
comment: .description Stores metadata and statistics about executed queries, such as start time, duration, error messages, resource usage, and other execution details. It does not store the results of queries.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: clickhouse_version
columns.comment: Version of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: system_processor
columns.comment: CPU architecture of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Type of an event that occurred when executing the query. Values: `QueryStart` — successful start of query execution, `QueryFinish` — successful end of query execution, `ExceptionBeforeStart` — exception before the start of query execution, `ExceptionWhileProcessing` — exception during the query execution.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Query starting date.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Query starting time.

columns.name: event_time_microseconds
columns.comment: Query starting time with microseconds precision.

columns.name: query_start_time
columns.comment: Start time of query execution.

columns.name: query_start_time_microseconds
columns.comment: Start time of query execution with microsecond precision.

columns.name: query_duration_ms
columns.comment: Duration of query execution in milliseconds.

columns.name: read_rows
columns.comment: Total number of rows read from all tables and table functions participated in query. It includes usual subqueries, subqueries for IN and JOIN. For distributed queries read_rows includes the total number of rows read at all replicas. Each replica sends it's read_rows value, and the server-initiator of the query summarizes all received and local values. The cache volumes do not affect this value.

columns.name: read_bytes
columns.comment: Total number of bytes read from all tables and table functions participated in query. It includes usual subqueries, subqueries for IN and JOIN. For distributed queries read_bytes includes the total number of rows read at all replicas. Each replica sends it's read_bytes value, and the server-initiator of the query summarizes all received and local values. The cache volumes do not affect this value.

columns.name: written_rows
columns.comment: The number of rows written by the query, including any rows written by downstream inserts triggered by the pipeline, such as attached materialized views. For a synchronous insert these downstream rows are recorded on the `query_kind` = `Insert` entry; for an asynchronous insert they are recorded on the `query_kind` = `AsyncInsertFlush` entry, while the client-facing `Insert` entry records only …

columns.name: written_bytes
columns.comment: The number of bytes written by the query (uncompressed), including any bytes written by downstream inserts triggered by the pipeline, such as attached materialized views. For a synchronous insert these downstream bytes are recorded on the `query_kind` = `Insert` entry; for an asynchronous insert they are recorded on the `query_kind` = `AsyncInsertFlush` entry, while the client-facing `Insert` e…

columns.name: result_rows
columns.comment: Number of rows in the result of a SELECT query, or the number of rows written by an insert. For a synchronous insert this includes rows written by downstream inserts triggered by the pipeline (such as attached materialized views) on the `query_kind` = `Insert` entry; for an asynchronous insert those downstream rows are recorded on the `query_kind` = `AsyncInsertFlush` entry, while the client-fa…

columns.name: result_bytes
columns.comment: RAM volume in bytes used to store a query result.

columns.name: memory_usage
columns.comment: Memory consumption by the query.

columns.name: current_database
columns.comment: Name of the current database.

columns.name: query
columns.comment: Query string.

columns.name: formatted_query
columns.comment: Formatted query string.

columns.name: normalized_query_hash
columns.comment: A numeric hash value, such as it is identical for queries differ only by values of literals.

columns.name: query_kind
columns.comment: Type of the query.

columns.name: databases
columns.comment: Names of the databases present in the query.

columns.name: tables
columns.comment: Names of the tables present in the query.

columns.name: columns
columns.comment: Names of the columns present in the query.

columns.name: partitions
columns.comment: Names of the partitions present in the query.

columns.name: projections
columns.comment: Names of the projections used during the query execution.

columns.name: views
columns.comment: Names of the (materialized or live) views present in the query.

columns.name: exception_code
columns.comment: Code of an exception.

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Exception message.

columns.name: stack_trace
columns.comment: Stack trace. An empty string, if the query was completed successfully.

columns.name: is_initial_query
columns.comment: Whether the query is initial. Possible values: 1 — an initial (top-level) query, 0 — a child query initiated by another query, including queries for distributed execution and internal subqueries.

columns.name: connection_address
columns.comment: The client IP address from which the connection was made. When connected through a proxy, this will be the address of the proxy.

columns.name: connection_port
columns.comment: The client port from which the connection was made. When connected through a proxy, this will be the port of the proxy.

columns.name: user
columns.comment: Name of the user who initiated the current query.

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: ID of the query.

columns.name: address
columns.comment: IP address that was used to make the query. When connected through a proxy and `auth_use_forwarded_address` is set, this will be the address of the client instead of the proxy.

columns.name: port
columns.comment: The client port that was used to make the query. When connected through a proxy and `auth_use_forwarded_address` is set, this will be the port of the client instead of the proxy.

columns.name: initial_user
columns.comment: Name of the user who ran the initial query in the same query chain.

columns.name: initial_query_id
columns.comment: ID of the initial query in the same query chain.

columns.name: initial_address
columns.comment: IP address from which the initial query in the same query chain was launched.

columns.name: initial_port
columns.comment: Client port from which the initial query in the same query chain was launched.

columns.name: initial_query_start_time
columns.comment: Start time of the initial query in the same query chain.

columns.name: initial_query_start_time_microseconds
columns.comment: Start time of the initial query in the same query chain, with microsecond precision.

columns.name: authenticated_user
columns.comment: Name of the user who was authenticated in the session.

columns.name: interface
columns.comment: Interface that the query was initiated from, as reported by the client. `Unknown` if the reported interface is not one this server recognizes.

columns.name: is_secure
columns.comment: The flag whether a query was executed over a secure interface

columns.name: os_user
columns.comment: Operating system username who runs clickhouse-client.

columns.name: client_hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the client machine where the clickhouse-client or another TCP client is run.

columns.name: client_name
columns.comment: The clickhouse-client or another TCP client name.

columns.name: client_agent
columns.comment: The AI coding agent that invoked the client (e.g. `claude-code`, `cursor`), detected from environment variables. Empty if no agent was detected.

columns.name: client_revision
columns.comment: Revision of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.name: client_version_major
columns.comment: Major version of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.name: client_version_minor
columns.comment: Minor version of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.name: client_version_patch
columns.comment: Patch component of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client version.

columns.name: script_query_number
columns.comment: The query number in a script with multiple queries for clickhouse-client.

columns.name: script_line_number
columns.comment: The line number of the query start in a script with multiple queries for clickhouse-client.

columns.name: http_method
columns.comment: HTTP method that initiated the query. `UNKNOWN` if the query did not arrive over HTTP, or if the reported method is not one this server recognizes.

columns.name: http_user_agent
columns.comment: HTTP header UserAgent passed in the HTTP query.

columns.name: http_referer
columns.comment: HTTP header Referer passed in the HTTP query (contains an absolute or partial address of the page making the query).

columns.name: forwarded_for
columns.comment: HTTP header X-Forwarded-For passed in the HTTP query.

columns.name: quota_key
columns.comment: The quota key specified in the quotas setting (see keyed).

columns.name: distributed_depth
columns.comment: How many times a query was forwarded between servers.

columns.name: revision
columns.comment: ClickHouse revision.

columns.name: http_handler_name
columns.comment: Name of the SQL-defined HTTP handler (CREATE HANDLER) that invoked the query. Empty if the query was not invoked through such a handler.

columns.name: http_request_url
columns.comment: The HTTP request path (without the query string) that invoked the query. The query string is omitted so that sensitive request parameters are not persisted. Empty for non-HTTP queries.

columns.name: log_comment
columns.comment: Log comment. It can be set to arbitrary string no longer than max_query_size. An empty string if it is not defined.

columns.name: thread_ids
columns.comment: Thread ids that are participating in query execution. These threads may not have run simultaneously.

columns.name: peak_threads_usage
columns.comment: Maximum count of simultaneous threads executing the query.

columns.name: ProfileEvents
columns.comment: ProfileEvents that measure different metrics. The description of them could be found in the table system.events

columns.name: Settings
columns.comment: Settings that were changed when the client ran the query. To enable logging changes to settings, set the log_query_settings parameter to 1.

columns.name: used_aggregate_functions
columns.comment: Canonical names of aggregate functions, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_aggregate_function_combinators
columns.comment: Canonical names of aggregate functions combinators, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_database_engines
columns.comment: Canonical names of database engines, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_data_type_families
columns.comment: Canonical names of data type families, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_dictionaries
columns.comment: Canonical names of dictionaries, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_formats
columns.comment: Canonical names of formats, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_functions
columns.comment: Canonical names of functions, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_storages
columns.comment: Canonical names of storages, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_table_functions
columns.comment: Canonical names of table functions, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_executable_user_defined_functions
columns.comment: Canonical names of executable user defined functions, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_sql_user_defined_functions
columns.comment: Canonical names of sql user defined functions, which were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_row_policies
columns.comment: The list of row policies names that were used during query execution.

columns.name: used_privileges
columns.comment: Privileges which were successfully checked during query execution.

columns.name: missing_privileges
columns.comment: Privileges that are missing during query execution.

columns.name: used_number_of_joins
columns.comment: The number of physical joins executed for this query. It is collected from the pipelines as they are built, so it reflects the joins that are left after all optimizations, not the number of JOIN clauses in the query text. A join is counted no matter how deeply it is nested: subqueries, common table expressions, views, views of views and the SELECT of a materialized view triggered by an INSERT a…

columns.name: used_join_algorithms
columns.comment: Algorithms of the joins counted in used_number_of_joins: 'HASH', 'PARALLEL_HASH', 'GRACE_HASH', 'PARTIAL_MERGE', 'FULL_SORTING_MERGE', 'PARALLEL_FULL_SORTING_MERGE', 'IE_JOIN', 'DIRECT', 'PASTE' and 'CONSTANT', sorted and deduplicated, so an algorithm shared by several joins appears once. This is the algorithm that was chosen to execute each join, not the algorithms that the join_algorithm sett…

columns.name: used_join_kinds
columns.comment: Kinds of the joins counted in used_number_of_joins, one element per join, so a kind shared by several joins appears several times. The elements are sorted rather than in execution order. Each kind is the one that was executed, which can differ from the query text, because the optimizer may run a join with its sides swapped and thereby turn LEFT into RIGHT.

columns.name: used_join_strictness
columns.comment: Strictness of the joins counted in used_number_of_joins, one element per join, in the same order as used_join_kinds: the element at a given index describes the same join in both arrays.

columns.name: spilled_to_disk
columns.comment: Operators that wrote data to temporary files on disk (processing in external memory) during query execution, sorted and deduplicated. An empty array means the query ran fully in memory.

columns.name: transaction_id
columns.comment: The identifier of the transaction in scope of which this query was executed.

columns.name: query_cache_usage
columns.comment: Usage of the query cache during query execution. Values: 'Unknown' = Status unknown, 'None' = The query result was neither written into nor read from the query result cache, 'Write' = The query result was written into the query result cache, 'Read' = The query result was read from the query result cache.

columns.name: asynchronous_read_counters
columns.comment: Metrics for asynchronous reading.

columns.name: is_internal
columns.comment: Indicates whether it is an auxiliary query executed internally.

name: query_metric_log
comment: .description Contains a history of memory and metric values from table `system.events` for individual queries, periodically flushed to disk.

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: Query ID.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: clickhouse_version
columns.comment: Version of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: system_processor
columns.comment: CPU architecture of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Event date.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Event time.

columns.name: event_time_microseconds
columns.comment: Event time with microseconds resolution.

columns.name: memory_usage
columns.comment: Amount of RAM the query uses. It might not include some types of dedicated memory.

columns.name: peak_memory_usage
columns.comment: Maximum amount of RAM the query used.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_Query
columns.comment: Number of queries to be interpreted and potentially executed. Does not include queries that failed to parse or were rejected due to AST size limits, quota limits or limits on the number of simultaneously running queries. May include internal queries initiated by ClickHouse itself. Does not count subqueries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_SelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as Query, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InsertQuery
columns.comment: Same as Query, but only for INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InitialQuery
columns.comment: Same as Query, but only counts initial queries (see is_initial_query).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InitialSelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as InitialQuery, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueriesWithSubqueries
columns.comment: Count queries with all subqueries

columns.name: ProfileEvent_SelectQueriesWithSubqueries
columns.comment: Count SELECT queries with all subqueries

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InsertQueriesWithSubqueries
columns.comment: Count INSERT queries with all subqueries

columns.name: ProfileEvent_SelectQueriesWithPrimaryKeyUsage
columns.comment: Count SELECT queries which use the primary key to evaluate the WHERE condition

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AsyncInsertQuery
columns.comment: Same as InsertQuery, but only for asynchronous INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AsyncInsertBytes
columns.comment: Data size in bytes of asynchronous INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AsyncInsertRows
columns.comment: Number of rows inserted by asynchronous INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AsyncInsertCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a duplicate hash id has been found in asynchronous INSERT hash id cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AsyncInsertFlush
columns.comment: Number of flushes of the asynchronous INSERT queue. Every flush inserts a batch of asynchronous INSERT queries as a single part. Compare with AsyncInsertQuery to see how many queries are batched together on average.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInternalQuery
columns.comment: Number of failed internal queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInternalSelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedInternalQuery, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInternalInsertQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedInternalQuery, but only for INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInitialQuery
columns.comment: Number of failed initial queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInitialSelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedInitialQuery, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedQuery
columns.comment: Number of total failed queries, both internal and user queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedSelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedQuery, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInsertQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedQuery, but only for INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedAsyncInsertQuery
columns.comment: Number of failed ASYNC INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerQueries
columns.comment: Number of fuzzed queries attempted by the server-side AST fuzzer.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerOracleChecks
columns.comment: Number of oracle checks attempted by the server-side AST fuzzer.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerOracleTLPAggregateChecks
columns.comment: Number of TLP Aggregate (State/Merge) oracle checks attempted by the server-side AST fuzzer.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerOracleMismatches
columns.comment: Number of oracle mismatches detected by the server-side AST fuzzer.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerSkippedBackupRestore
columns.comment: Number of fuzzed BACKUP/RESTORE queries the server-side AST fuzzer skipped instead of executing.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerSkippedReplicatedDDLInternal
columns.comment: Number of times the server-side AST fuzzer skipped fuzzing because an internal replicated-database DDL execution (a live ZooKeeperMetadataTransaction) was in flight on the context.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerSkippedCollaborativeWorker
columns.comment: Number of times the server-side AST fuzzer skipped fuzzing because the context was executing as a collaborative worker for another node's query: a parallel replicas participant or a cluster function worker.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerSkippedSecondaryQuery
columns.comment: Number of times the server-side AST fuzzer skipped fuzzing because the query was a secondary query sent by another node.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time of all queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_SelectQueryTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time of SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InsertQueryTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time of INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OtherQueryTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time of queries that are not SELECT or INSERT.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FileOpen
columns.comment: Number of files opened.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_Seek
columns.comment: Number of times the 'lseek' function was called.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorRead
columns.comment: Number of reads (read/pread) from a file descriptor. Does not include sockets.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorReadFailed
columns.comment: Number of times the read (read/pread) from a file descriptor have failed.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorReadBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read from file descriptors. If the file is compressed, this will show the compressed data size.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorPageCacheHitBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read from file descriptors with the synchronous `pread` that were detected to be served from the OS page cache (this is done only for the reads with a bandwidth throttler).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWrite
columns.comment: Number of writes (write/pwrite) to a file descriptor. Does not include sockets.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWriteFailed
columns.comment: Number of times the write (write/pwrite) to a file descriptor have failed.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWriteBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes written to file descriptors. If the file is compressed, this will show compressed data size.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FileSync
columns.comment: Number of times the F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync function was called for files.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DirectorySync
columns.comment: Number of times the F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync function was called for directories.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FileSyncElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync syscall for files.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DirectorySyncElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync syscall for directories.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadCompressedBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes (the number of bytes before decompression) read from compressed sources (files, network).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferBlocks
columns.comment: Number of compressed blocks (the blocks of data that are compressed independent of each other) read from compressed sources (files, network).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferBytes
columns.comment: Number of uncompressed bytes (the number of bytes after decompression) read from compressed sources (files, network).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferChecksumDoesntMatch
columns.comment: Number of times the compressed block checksum did not match.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferChecksumDoesntMatchSingleBitMismatch
columns.comment: Number of times a compressed block checksum mismatch was caused by a single-bit difference.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferChecksumDoesntMatchMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent detecting bit-flips due to compressed block checksum mismatches.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UncompressedCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a block of data has been found in the uncompressed cache (and decompression was avoided).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UncompressedCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a block of data has not been found in the uncompressed cache (and required decompression).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UncompressedCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Number of bytes evicted from the uncompressed cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a block of data has been found in the userspace page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a block of data has not been found in the userspace page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Number of bytes evicted from the userspace page cache

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheResized
columns.comment: Number of times the userspace page cache was auto-resized (typically happens a few times per second, controlled by memory_worker_period_ms).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheOvercommitResize
columns.comment: Number of times the userspace page cache was auto-resized to free memory during a memory allocation.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheReadBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read from userspace page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MMappedFileCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a file has been found in the MMap cache (for the 'mmap' read_method), so we didn't have to mmap it again.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MMappedFileCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a file has not been found in the MMap cache (for the 'mmap' read_method), so we had to mmap it again.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OpenedFileCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a file has been found in the opened file cache, so we didn't have to open it again.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OpenedFileCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a file has been found in the opened file cache, so we had to open it again.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OpenedFileCacheMicroseconds
columns.comment: Amount of time spent executing OpenedFileCache methods.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AIOWrite
columns.comment: Number of writes with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AIOWriteBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes written with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AIORead
columns.comment: Number of reads with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AIOReadBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IOBufferAllocs
columns.comment: Number of allocations of IO buffers (for ReadBuffer/WriteBuffer).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IOBufferAllocBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes allocated for IO buffers (for ReadBuffer/WriteBuffer).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ArenaAllocChunks
columns.comment: Number of chunks allocated for memory Arena (used for GROUP BY and similar operations)

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ArenaAllocBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes allocated for memory Arena (used for GROUP BY and similar operations)

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FiberStackAllocs
columns.comment: Number of stacks allocated for fibers (fibers are used for asynchronous communication with remote replicas).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FiberStackAllocBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes allocated for fiber stacks, including guard pages (guard pages are only used in debug and sanitizer builds).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FiberStackAllocNanoseconds
columns.comment: Amount of time spent allocating fiber stacks. Nanoseconds are used because a single allocation is normally faster than a microsecond, unless the allocator or the kernel is contended.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FiberStackFreeNanoseconds
columns.comment: Amount of time spent deallocating fiber stacks.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FunctionExecute
columns.comment: Number of SQL ordinary function calls (SQL functions are called on per-block basis, so this number represents the number of blocks).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TableFunctionExecute
columns.comment: Number of table function calls.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DatabaseTablesEnumerated
columns.comment: Number of tables a database handed out through its table iterator - to `SHOW TABLES`, the system tables that list tables and everything else that walks a database. A condition on the table name in a query over such a system table narrows the enumeration, and this counter shows by how much.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DefaultImplementationForNullsRows
columns.comment: Number of rows processed by default implementation for nulls in function execution

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DefaultImplementationForNullsRowsWithNulls
columns.comment: Number of rows which contain null values processed by default implementation for nulls in function execution

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MarkCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has been found in the mark cache, so we didn't have to load a mark file.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MarkCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has not been found in the mark cache, so we had to load a mark file in memory, which is a costly operation, adding to query latency.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UniqueKeyBitmapLoadMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent reading and deserializing UNIQUE KEY delete-bitmap sidecar files on a DeleteBitmapCache miss.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UniqueKeyMutexHoldMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total wall-clock time the per-partition UNIQUE KEY mutex was held across all acquisitions on this server (sum of hold-time microseconds).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UniqueKeyDedupProbes
columns.comment: Number of new-row keys probed against existing parts on the UNIQUE KEY INSERT write-path.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UniqueKeyConflictOverwriteRows
columns.comment: Number of new-row keys that superseded a live row in an existing part on the UNIQUE KEY INSERT write-path.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UniqueKeyConflictIgnoredRows
columns.comment: Number of incoming rows dropped by unique_key_conflict_action = ignore because the key was already live in the partition.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PrimaryIndexCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has been found in the primary index cache, so we didn't have to load a index file.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_StatisticsCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times the statistics of a column of a data part have been found in the statistics cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_StatisticsCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times the statistics of a column of a data part have not been found in the statistics cache, so they had to be loaded from the part.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PrimaryIndexCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has not been found in the primary index cache, so we had to load a index file in memory, which is a costly operation, adding to query latency.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataFilesCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times iceberg metadata files have been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataFilesCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times iceberg metadata files have not been found in the iceberg metadata cache and had to be read from (remote) disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataFilesCacheStaleMisses
columns.comment: Number of times iceberg metadata files have been found in the cache, but were considered stale and had to be read from (remote) disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataFilesCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Approximate number of bytes evicted from the iceberg metadata cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PaimonMetadataFilesCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times paimon metadata files have been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PaimonMetadataFilesCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times paimon metadata files have not been found in the paimon metadata cache and had to be read from (remote) disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PaimonMetadataFilesCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Approximate number of bytes evicted from the paimon metadata cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TimeSeriesMetricFamiliesDeduplicationCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of rows not written to the metric families tables of TimeSeries tables because the deduplication cache already had them or the same insert had already written them.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TimeSeriesMetricFamiliesDeduplicationCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of rows written to the metric families tables of TimeSeries tables after they were not found in the deduplication cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TimeSeriesTagsDeduplicationCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of rows not written to the tags tables of TimeSeries tables because the deduplication cache already had them or the same insert had already written them.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TimeSeriesTagsDeduplicationCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of rows written to the tags tables of TimeSeries tables after they were not found in the deduplication cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataReadWaitTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time data readers spend waiting for iceberg metadata files to be read and parsed, summed across all reader threads.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParquetMetadataCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times parquet metadata has been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParquetMetadataCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times parquet metadata has not been found in the cache and had to be read from disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParquetMetadataCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Approximate number of bytes evicted from the parquet metadata cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergIteratorInitializationMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent on synchronous initialization of iceberg data iterators.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataUpdateMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent updating iceberg storage metadata from state (buildStorageMetadataFromState).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataReturnedObjectInfos
columns.comment: Total number of returned object infos from iceberg iterator.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMinMaxNonPrunedDeleteFiles
columns.comment: Total number of accepted data files-position delete file pairs by minmax analysis from pairs suitable by partitioning and sequence number.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMinMaxPrunedDeleteFiles
columns.comment: Total number of accepted data files-position delete file pairs by minmax analysis from pairs suitable by partitioning and sequence number.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergCompactionCleanupDeferredByReaders
columns.comment: Number of times the removal of data files superseded by Iceberg compaction was postponed because a query on this or another replica was still reading a snapshot that references them.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergCompactionCleanupDeferredBySnapshotLifetime
columns.comment: Number of times the removal of data files superseded by Iceberg compaction was postponed because the compaction or a snapshot it superseded was fresher than `iceberg_outdated_snapshot_lifetime_seconds`.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ObjectStorageSharedLeasesAcquired
columns.comment: Number of shared leases of keys, such as Iceberg snapshots being read, written to object storage when a query of this server acquired a key that was not leased by the server yet.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ObjectStorageSharedLeasesRenewed
columns.comment: Number of shared leases rewritten in object storage by the renewal task while the queries of this server held the key.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ObjectStorageSharedLeasesRefused
columns.comment: Number of attempts to lease a key in object storage refused because a cleaner condemned the key, such as an Iceberg snapshot about to be removed by the cleanup after a compaction.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ObjectStorageSharedLeaseWriteFailures
columns.comment: Number of failed writes of shared leases to object storage, on acquisition or on renewal.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ObjectStorageSharedLeasesCondemned
columns.comment: Number of keys condemned in object storage by a cleaner of this server, so that no replica leases them while it removes what they protect.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ObjectStorageExclusiveLeasesAcquired
columns.comment: Number of exclusive leases of keys, such as the compaction of an Iceberg table, acquired in object storage by this server.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ObjectStorageExclusiveLeasesRefused
columns.comment: Number of attempts to acquire an exclusive lease in object storage given up because another replica held a live lease of the key.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ObjectStorageExpiredLeasesRemoved
columns.comment: Number of expired lease objects and condemned markers removed from object storage.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DeltaLakeDeltaLogExistenceChecks
columns.comment: Number of object-storage listings issued to check whether a DeltaLake `_delta_log` exists (e.g. during CREATE TABLE).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OneLakeAccessTokenRequests
columns.comment: Number of access token requests issued by the OneLake catalog via the Entra ID refresh token grant.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OneLakeAccessTokenRequestFailures
columns.comment: Number of failed access token requests issued by the OneLake catalog via the Entra ID refresh token grant (including expired or revoked refresh tokens).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OneLakeAccessTokenRequestMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent requesting access tokens via the Entra ID refresh token grant in the OneLake catalog.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OneLakeAccessTokenExpirations
columns.comment: Number of times the cached OneLake access token was found expired and renewed transparently.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_VectorSimilarityIndexCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times an index granule has been found in the vector index cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_VectorSimilarityIndexCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times an index granule has not been found in the vector index cache and had to be read from disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_VectorSimilarityIndexCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Approximate number of bytes evicted from the vector index cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReadDictionaryBlocks
columns.comment: Number of times a text index dictionary block has been read from disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexTokensCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a text index token info has been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexTokensCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a text index token info has not been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexTokensCacheNegativeHits
columns.comment: Number of times an absent text index token has been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexTokensCacheNegativeMisses
columns.comment: Number of absent text index tokens added to the cache after a dictionary lookup.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexHeaderCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a header has been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexHeaderCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a header has not been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPostingsCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a text index posting list has been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPostingsCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a text index posting list has not been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReadSparseIndexBlocks
columns.comment: Number of times a sparse index block has been read from the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReaderTotalMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent reading the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReadGranulesMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent reading and analyzing granules of the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPositionsDecodeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent decoding text index position lists (.pos) for phrase search.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPhraseMatchMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent matching phrase positions over candidate rows.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPositionsBlocksRead
columns.comment: Number of position blocks read to match phrase queries over a text index. A block spanning two candidate windows is counted once per read.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPositionsBlocksTotal
columns.comment: Number of total position blocks of the phrase tokens before selecting which ones to read.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPositionsBytesRead
columns.comment: Bytes of position blocks read to match phrase queries over a text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPhraseCandidates
columns.comment: Candidate rows (postings intersection) examined by candidate-driven phrase search.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPhraseSearches
columns.comment: Number of phrase searches executed over a text index. Repeated searches of the same phrase in the same part are served from the cache and are not counted.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPhraseFallbacks
columns.comment: Number of times a phrase query skipped the text index because the phrase was estimated to match more rows than 'text_index_hint_max_selectivity', and was evaluated on the column instead.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReadPostings
columns.comment: Number of times a posting list has been read from the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexUsedEmbeddedPostings
columns.comment: Number of times a posting list embedded in the dictionary has been used.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexUseHint
columns.comment: Number of index granules where a direct reading from the text index was added as hint and was used.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexDiscardHint
columns.comment: Number of index granules where a direct reading from the text index was added as hint and was discarded due to low selectivity.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexTemporarySegmentsWritten
columns.comment: Number of temporary segments written while building text indexes.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyPackedBlocksDecoded
columns.comment: Number of packed blocks decoded in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyAdvanceCount
columns.comment: Number of advance operations performed in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazySegmentsPrepared
columns.comment: Number of segments prepared (read from disk or cached) in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazySegmentsBuilt
columns.comment: Number of segments actually read and decoded (cache misses) in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyBruteForceIntersections
columns.comment: Number of brute-force intersections performed in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyLeapfrogIntersections
columns.comment: Number of leapfrog intersections performed in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyBruteForceEarlyExits
columns.comment: Number of brute-force intersections in lazy posting list mode that stopped early because no row of the window was left in all the posting lists applied so far, so the intersection is empty.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazySegmentsSkippedDense
columns.comment: Number of fully-dense segments padded as a whole (memset for OR, increment for AND) instead of decoding blocks, in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazySegmentsSkippedResolved
columns.comment: Number of segments skipped because the output region was already resolved (all-ones for OR, no row left in all the posting lists applied so far for AND) in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyBlocksSkippedResolved
columns.comment: Number of packed blocks skipped because the output region was already resolved (all-ones for OR, no row left in all the posting lists applied so far for AND) in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyBlocksSkippedDense
columns.comment: Number of packed blocks of consecutive row ids padded as a whole (memset for OR, increment for AND) instead of being decoded, in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexDiscardPatternScan
columns.comment: Number of times pattern-based dictionary scan in a text index was discarded because the number of posting lists to read exceeded the threshold.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPatternBypassCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a text index pattern dictionary scan was skipped because an earlier scan of the same part exceeded the posting-list threshold.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexGenericExclusionSearchAlgorithm
columns.comment: Number of times the generic exclusion search algorithm is used over the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexGenericExclusionSearchStepLimitReached
columns.comment: Number of times the generic exclusion search over the text index reached merge_tree_generic_exclusion_search_max_steps and accepted the remaining mark ranges without further splitting.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryConditionCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has been found in the query condition cache (and reading of marks can be skipped). Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_condition_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryConditionCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has not been found in the query condition cache (and reading of mark cannot be skipped). Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_condition_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_EncryptionHeaderCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times encryption header bytes were found in the encryption header cache, so the source read of the header was skipped.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_EncryptionHeaderCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times encryption header bytes were not found in the encryption header cache, so they were read from the source.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a query result has been found in the query cache (and query computation was avoided). Counts the query cache as a whole: a miss in memory followed by a hit in the query cache on disk is one hit. Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a query result has not been found in the query cache (and required query computation). Counts the query cache as a whole: a query is a miss only if it was found in neither the in-memory nor the on-disk backend. Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheOnDiskHits
columns.comment: Number of times a query result has been found in the query cache on disk (see setting query_cache_on_disk_cache_name), the breakdown of the on-disk backend of QueryCacheHits. Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheOnDiskMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a query result has not been found in the query cache on disk (see setting query_cache_on_disk_cache_name), the breakdown of the on-disk backend of QueryCacheMisses. Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheOnDiskReadBytes
columns.comment: Number of serialized (compressed) bytes read from the query cache on disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheOnDiskWrittenBytes
columns.comment: Number of serialized (compressed) bytes written into the query cache on disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheAgeSeconds
columns.comment: The sum of ages of found query cache entries in seconds. Only updated for hits, of both the in-memory and the on-disk backend of the query cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheReadRows
columns.comment: The number of rows read from the query cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheReadBytes
columns.comment: The number of (uncompressed) bytes read from the query cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheWrittenRows
columns.comment: The number of rows saved into the query cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheWrittenBytes
columns.comment: The number of (uncompressed) bytes saved into the query cache

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferOrdinary
columns.comment: Number of times ordinary read buffer was created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferDirectIO
columns.comment: Number of times a read buffer with O_DIRECT was created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferDirectIOFailed
columns.comment: Number of times a read buffer with O_DIRECT was attempted to be created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods), but the OS did not allow it (due to lack of filesystem support or other reasons) and we fallen back to the ordinary reading method.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferMMap
columns.comment: Number of times a read buffer using 'mmap' was created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferMMapFailed
columns.comment: Number of times a read buffer with 'mmap' was attempted to be created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods), but the OS did not allow it (due to lack of filesystem support or other reasons) and we fallen back to the ordinary reading method.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskReadElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for read syscall. This include reads from page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskWriteElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for write syscall. This include writes to page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NetworkReceiveElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for data to receive or receiving data from network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NetworkSendElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for data to send to network or sending data to network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NetworkReceiveBytes
columns.comment: Total number of bytes received from network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NetworkSendBytes
columns.comment: Total number of bytes send to network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NativeProtocolSend
columns.comment: Number of non-empty native protocol output buffer flushes.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FilterPartsByVirtualColumnsMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent in filterPartsByVirtualColumns function.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolExpansions
columns.comment: Counts the total number of times new threads have been added to the global thread pool. This metric indicates the frequency of expansions in the global thread pool to accommodate increased processing demands.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolShrinks
columns.comment: Counts the total number of times the global thread pool has shrunk by removing threads. This occurs when the number of idle threads exceeds max_thread_pool_free_size, indicating adjustments in the global thread pool size in response to decreased thread utilization.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolThreadCreationMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for new threads to start.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolLockWaitMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time threads have spent waiting for locks in the global thread pool.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolJobs
columns.comment: Counts the number of jobs that have been pushed to the global thread pool.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolJobWaitTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Measures the elapsed time from when a job is scheduled in the thread pool to when it is picked up for execution by a worker thread. This metric helps identify delays in job processing, indicating the responsiveness of the thread pool to new tasks.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolExpansions
columns.comment: Counts the total number of times threads have been borrowed from the global thread pool to expand local thread pools.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolShrinks
columns.comment: Counts the total number of times threads have been returned to the global thread pool from local thread pools.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolThreadCreationMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time local thread pools have spent waiting to borrow a thread from the global pool.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolLockWaitMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time threads have spent waiting for locks in the local thread pools.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolJobs
columns.comment: Counts the number of jobs that have been pushed to the local thread pools.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolBusyMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time threads have spent executing the actual work.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolJobWaitTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Measures the elapsed time from when a job is scheduled in the thread pool to when it is picked up for execution by a worker thread. This metric helps identify delays in job processing, indicating the responsiveness of the thread pool to new tasks.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3GetRequestThrottlerCount
columns.comment: Number of DiskS3 GET and SELECT requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3GetRequestThrottlerBlocked
columns.comment: Number of DiskS3 GET and SELECT requests blocked by throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3GetRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform DiskS3 GET and SELECT request throttling.

columns.comment: Number of DiskS3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST requests blocked by throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3PutRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform DiskS3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST request throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3GetRequestThrottlerCount
columns.comment: Number of S3 GET and SELECT requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3GetRequestThrottlerBlocked
columns.comment: Number of S3 GET and SELECT requests blocked by throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3GetRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform S3 GET and SELECT request throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3PutRequestThrottlerCount
columns.comment: Number of S3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3PutRequestThrottlerBlocked
columns.comment: Number of S3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST requests blocked by throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3PutRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform S3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST request throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ACMEAPIRequests
columns.comment: Number of ACME API requests issued.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ACMECertificateOrders
columns.comment: Number of ACME certificate orders issued.

columns.comment: Number of Azure disk read requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureReadRequestsErrors

columns.comment: Number of Azure disk read requests throttled.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureReadRequestsRedirects

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureWriteRequestsRedirects

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureReadRequestsCount
columns.comment: Number of Azure read requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureWriteMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for Azure write requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureWriteRequestsCount
columns.comment: Number of Azure write requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureWriteRequestsErrors
columns.comment: Number of Azure write request errors.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureWriteRequestsThrottling
columns.comment: Number of Azure write requests throttled.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureWriteRequestsRedirects

columns.comment: Number of Azure GET requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.comment: Number of Azure GET requests blocked by throttler.

columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform Azure GET request throttling.

columns.comment: Number of Azure disk GET requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.comment: Number of Azure disk PUT requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.comment: Number of Azure disk PUT requests blocked by throttler.

columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform Azure disk PUT request throttling.

columns.comment: Bytes passed through 'max_remote_write_network_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_remote_write_network_bandwidth' throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalWriteThrottlerBytes
columns.comment: Bytes passed through 'max_local_write_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_local_write_bandwidth' throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalWriteThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform 'max_local_write_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_local_write_bandwidth' throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_BackupThrottlerBytes
columns.comment: Bytes passed through 'max_backup_bandwidth_for_server' throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_BackupThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform 'max_backup_bandwidth_for_server' throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MergesThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform 'max_merges_bandwidth_for_server' throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MutationsThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform 'max_mutations_bandwidth_for_server' throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReaderExecutorDecryptMicroseconds

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReaderExecutorModeledCostMicroseconds

Divide by ReaderExecutorDeliveredBytes for a load-…
