columns.name: ProfileEvent_SystemTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent in processing (queries and other tasks) threads executing CPU instructions in OS kernel mode. This is time spent in syscalls, excluding waiting time during blocking syscalls.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MemoryOvercommitWaitTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent in waiting for memory to be freed in OvercommitTracker.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MemoryAllocatorPurge
columns.comment: Total number of times memory allocator purge was requested

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MemoryAllocatorPurgeTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent for memory allocator purge

columns.name: ProfileEvent_SoftPageFaults
columns.comment: The number of soft page faults in query execution threads. Soft page fault usually means a miss in the memory allocator cache, which requires a new memory mapping from the OS and subsequent allocation of a page of physical memory.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_HardPageFaults
columns.comment: The number of hard page faults in query execution threads. High values indicate either that you forgot to turn off swap on your server, or eviction of memory pages of the ClickHouse binary during very high memory pressure, or successful usage of the 'mmap' read method for the tables data.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OSIOWaitMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a thread spent waiting for a result of IO operation, from the OS point of view. This is real IO that doesn't include page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OSCPUWaitMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a thread was ready for execution but waiting to be scheduled by OS, from the OS point of view.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OSCPUVirtualTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: CPU time spent seen by OS. Does not include involuntary waits due to virtualization.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OSReadBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read from disks or block devices. Doesn't include bytes read from page cache. May include excessive data due to block size, readahead, etc.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OSWriteBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes written to disks or block devices. Doesn't include bytes that are in page cache dirty pages. May not include data that was written by OS asynchronously.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OSReadChars
columns.comment: Number of bytes read from filesystem, including page cache, as well as network and other files.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OSWriteChars
columns.comment: Number of bytes written to filesystem, including page cache, as well as network and other files.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasHandleRequestMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent processing requests for marks from replicas

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasHandleAnnouncementMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent processing replicas announcements

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasAnnouncementMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent to send an announcement

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasReadRequestMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent for read requests

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasReadAssignedMarks
columns.comment: Sum across all replicas of how many of scheduled marks were assigned by consistent hash

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasReadUnassignedMarks
columns.comment: Sum across all replicas of how many unassigned marks were scheduled

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasReadAssignedForStealingMarks
columns.comment: Sum across all replicas of how many of scheduled marks were assigned for stealing by consistent hash

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasReadMarks
columns.comment: How many marks were read by the given replica

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadPoolRangeRefinerDroppedMarks
columns.comment: How many marks were dropped from read tasks by a ranges refiner in MergeTree read pools (e.g. marks fully filtered out by a projection index)

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadPoolRangeRefinerDroppedCuts
columns.comment: How many times ranges cut from a part by a MergeTree read pool were fully dropped by a ranges refiner, so no read task was created for them

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasStealingByHashMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent collecting segments meant for stealing by hash

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasProcessingPartsMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent processing data parts

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasStealingLeftoversMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent collecting orphaned segments

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasCollectingOwnedSegmentsMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent collecting segments meant by hash

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParallelReplicasNumRequests
columns.comment: Number of requests to the initiator.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CacheWarmerBytesDownloaded
columns.comment: Amount of data fetched into filesystem cache by dedicated background threads.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CacheWarmerDataPartsDownloaded
columns.comment: Number of data parts that were fully fetched by CacheWarmer.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IgnoredColdParts
columns.comment: See setting ignore_cold_parts_seconds. Number of times read queries ignored very new parts that weren't pulled into cache by CacheWarmer yet.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PreferredWarmedUnmergedParts
columns.comment: See setting prefer_warmed_unmerged_parts_seconds. Number of times read queries used outdated pre-merge parts that are in cache instead of merged part that wasn't pulled into cache by CacheWarmer yet.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCPUCycles
columns.comment: Total cycles. Be wary of what happens during CPU frequency scaling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfInstructions
columns.comment: Retired instructions. Be careful, these can be affected by various issues, most notably hardware interrupt counts.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCacheReferences
columns.comment: Cache accesses. Usually, this indicates Last Level Cache accesses, but this may vary depending on your CPU. This may include prefetches and coherency messages; again this depends on the design of your CPU.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCacheMisses
columns.comment: Cache misses. Usually this indicates Last Level Cache misses; this is intended to be used in conjunction with the PERFCOUNTHWCACHEREFERENCES event to calculate cache miss rates.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfBranchInstructions
columns.comment: Retired branch instructions. Prior to Linux 2.6.35, this used the wrong event on AMD processors.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfBranchMisses
columns.comment: Mispredicted branch instructions.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfBusCycles
columns.comment: Bus cycles, which can be different from total cycles.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfStalledCyclesFrontend
columns.comment: Stalled cycles during issue.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfStalledCyclesBackend
columns.comment: Stalled cycles during retirement.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfRefCPUCycles
columns.comment: Total cycles; not affected by CPU frequency scaling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCPUClock
columns.comment: The CPU clock, a high-resolution per-CPU timer

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfTaskClock
columns.comment: A clock count specific to the task that is running

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfContextSwitches
columns.comment: Number of context switches

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCPUMigrations
columns.comment: Number of times the process has migrated to a new CPU

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfAlignmentFaults
columns.comment: Number of alignment faults. These happen when unaligned memory accesses happen; the kernel can handle these but it reduces performance. This happens only on some architectures (never on x86).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfEmulationFaults
columns.comment: Number of emulation faults. The kernel sometimes traps on unimplemented instructions and emulates them for user space. This can negatively impact performance.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfMinEnabledTime
columns.comment: For all events, minimum time that an event was enabled. Used to track event multiplexing influence

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfMinEnabledRunningTime
columns.comment: Running time for event with minimum enabled time. Used to track the amount of event multiplexing

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfDataTLBReferences
columns.comment: Data TLB references

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfDataTLBMisses
columns.comment: Data TLB misses

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfInstructionTLBReferences
columns.comment: Instruction TLB references

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfInstructionTLBMisses
columns.comment: Instruction TLB misses

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfLocalMemoryReferences
columns.comment: Local NUMA node memory reads

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfLocalMemoryMisses
columns.comment: Local NUMA node memory read misses

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CannotWriteToWriteBufferDiscard
columns.comment: Number of stack traces dropped by query profiler or signal handler because pipe is full or cannot write to pipe.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryProfilerSignalOverruns
columns.comment: Number of times we drop processing of a query profiler signal due to overrun plus the number of signals that OS has not delivered due to overrun.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryProfilerConcurrencyOverruns
columns.comment: Number of times we drop processing of a query profiler signal due to too many concurrent query profilers in other threads, which may indicate overload.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryProfilerRuns
columns.comment: Number of times QueryProfiler had been run.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryProfilerErrors
columns.comment: Invalid memory accesses during asynchronous stack unwinding.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedLogEntryForMerge
columns.comment: Successfully created log entry to merge parts in ReplicatedMergeTree.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NotCreatedLogEntryForMerge
columns.comment: Log entry to merge parts in ReplicatedMergeTree is not created due to concurrent log update by another replica.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedLogEntryForMutation
columns.comment: Successfully created log entry to mutate parts in ReplicatedMergeTree.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NotCreatedLogEntryForMutation
columns.comment: Log entry to mutate parts in ReplicatedMergeTree is not created due to concurrent log update by another replica.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3WriteRequestRetryableErrors

columns.comment: Number of directories created by the 'plain_rewritable' metadata storage for AzureObjectStorage.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskPlainRewritableAzureDirectoryRemoved
columns.comment: Number of directories removed by the 'plain_rewritable' metadata storage for AzureObjectStorage.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskPlainRewritableLocalDirectoryRemoved

columns.comment: Number of directories created by the 'plain_rewritable' metadata storage for S3ObjectStorage.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskPlainRewritableS3DirectoryRemoved
columns.comment: Number of directories removed by the 'plain_rewritable' metadata storage for S3ObjectStorage.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskPlainRewritableLegacyLayoutDiskCount
columns.comment: Number of the 'plain_rewritable' disks with legacy layout.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskPlainRewritableOrphanedObjectsRemoved
columns.comment: Number of objects deleted by the 'plain_rewritable' metadata storage while loading, because they were left by removals that a previous server process had committed but not finished (for example, it was killed during DROP TABLE).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskPlainRewritableUndoStageRetries
columns.comment: Number of times a step of reversing a failed 'plain_rewritable' metadata transaction had to be repeated because object storage rejected it.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MetadataTransactionRollbacks
columns.comment: Number of metadata transactions that failed to commit and were rolled back.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MetadataTransactionRollbacksFailed
columns.comment: Number of metadata transaction rollbacks that did not run to completion, so the metadata keeps a part of a transaction that was reported as failed.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3Clients
columns.comment: Number of created S3 clients.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TinyS3Clients
columns.comment: Number of S3 clients copies which reuse an existing auth provider from another client.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ElasticsearchPointInTimeCloseFailures
columns.comment: Number of failed attempts to close an Elasticsearch point in time.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_EngineFileLikeReadFiles
columns.comment: Number of files read in table engines working with files (like File/S3/URL/HDFS).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromS3Microseconds

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromS3InitMicroseconds

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromS3Bytes

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromS3RequestsErrors
columns.comment: Number of exceptions while reading from S3.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromS3RequestsCut
columns.comment: Number of requests from S3 disks cut to one buffer fill because the connection group of the disks was at or above `disk_connections_soft_limit`.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromS3Microseconds
columns.comment: Time spent on writing to S3.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromS3Bytes
columns.comment: Bytes written to S3.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromS3RequestsErrors
columns.comment: Number of exceptions while writing to S3.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromS3WaitInflightLimitMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent on waiting while some of the current requests are done when its number reached the limit defined by s3_max_inflight_parts_for_one_file.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryMemoryLimitExceeded
columns.comment: Number of times when memory limit exceeded for query.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalMemoryLimitExceeded
columns.comment: Number of times the global memory limit was exceeded.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MemoryAllocatedWithoutCheck
columns.comment: Number of times memory has been allocated without checking for memory constraints.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MemoryAllocatedWithoutCheckBytes
columns.comment: Amount of bytes that has been allocated without checking for memory constraints.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryMemoryDriftSettled
columns.comment: Number of queries that ended with memory still charged to them (or over-credited). The difference is taken off the per-user tracker, so that it ends at zero for the query.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryMemoryDriftSettledBytes
columns.comment: Absolute amount of bytes taken off per-user trackers when queries ended, that is, how far per-query accounting was off.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MemoryLargeAllocationTraced
columns.comment: Number of times a stack trace was captured for a single charge to the global memory tracker at or above `min_allocation_size_to_log_stack_trace`.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CachedReadBufferCacheWriteStopped

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CachedReadBufferCreateBufferMicroseconds
columns.comment: Prepare buffer time

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CachedWriteBufferCacheWriteBytes
columns.comment: Bytes written from source (remote fs, etc) to filesystem cache

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CachedWriteBufferCacheWriteMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent writing data into filesystem cache

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CachedWriteBufferCacheWriteStopped
columns.comment: Number of times write-through caching was stopped (space reservation or the cache write failed, or a covering segment was being evicted), after which the write continues without populating the cache

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CachedWriteBufferCoveringSegmentShrunk

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CachedWriteBufferCoveringSegmentShrinkFailed

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FilesystemCachePriorityReadLockMicroseconds
columns.comment: Lock filesystem cache time for read in priority queue

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FilesystemCacheStateLockMicroseconds

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AdaptiveAggregationStagedChunkPiecesOverBound
columns.comment: How many pieces of a cut staged chunk the adaptive aggregation published still over the bound the chunk was cut to meet. A chunk is cut along bucket boundaries, and record by record inside a bucket that is over the bound on its own, so this is a single record whose staged bytes alone are over the bound; such a piece is claimed whole, and its drain can overshoot the pressure part by that much.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AdaptiveAggregationStagedClaimsClosedAtBound
columns.comment: How many claims of staged chunks by the adaptive aggregation's drains were closed before a chunk whose addition would have taken the batch to the pressure part bound, leaving that chunk to the next claim. columns.name: ProfileEvent_AggregationTopKKeysPruned
columns.comment: How many evicted grouping keys were also erased from the intermediate hash table, with their aggregate states destroyed (see `enable_group_by_top_k_optimization`). Lower than `AggregationTopKKeysEvicted` when the aggregation method cannot erase keys, or when only a prefix of the key is ranked: the heap then still skips rows, but the hash table keeps every admitted group.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AggregationTopKHeapsFrozen
columns.comment: How many top-K aggregation heaps were frozen, falling back to regular aggregation. Either the heap rejected almost nothing within its observation window (e.g. the number of distinct grouping keys does not exceed the LIMIT), or a tie-set at the heap's boundary - which can never be evicted - overgrew it (see `enable_group_by_top_k_optimization`).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TopKGranulesSkippedByPrimaryKey

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DistinctTransformsSwitchedToPassThrough

Settings that switch automatic parallel replicas off altogether are not counted: with `enable_parallel_replicas` disabled or forced, or `parallel_replicas_mode` other than `read_tasks`, the op…

name: replicas
comment: .description Contains information and status for replicated tables residing on the local server. This table can be used for monitoring. The table contains a row for every Replicated\* table.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Database name.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: uuid
columns.comment: Table UUID.

columns.name: engine
columns.comment: Table engine name.

columns.name: is_leader
columns.comment: Whether the replica is the leader. Multiple replicas can be leaders at the same time. A replica can be prevented from becoming a leader using the merge_tree setting replicated_can_become_leader. The leaders are responsible for scheduling background merges. Note that writes can be performed to any replica that is available and has a session in ZK, regardless of whether it is a leader.

columns.name: can_become_leader
columns.comment: Whether the replica can be a leader.

columns.name: is_readonly
columns.comment: Whether the replica is in read-only mode. This mode is turned on if the config does not have sections with ClickHouse Keeper, if an unknown error occurred when reinitializing sessions in ClickHouse Keeper, and during session reinitialization in ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: readonly_start_time
columns.comment: The timestamp when the replica transitioned into readonly mode. Null if the replica is not in readonly mode.

columns.name: is_session_expired
columns.comment: Whether the session with ClickHouse Keeper has expired. Basically the same as `is_readonly`.

columns.name: future_parts
columns.comment: The number of data parts that will appear as the result of INSERTs or merges that haven't been done yet.

columns.name: parts_to_check
columns.comment: The number of data parts in the queue for verification. A part is put in the verification queue if there is suspicion that it might be damaged.

columns.name: zookeeper_name
columns.comment: The name of the [Zoo]Keeper cluster (possibly auxiliary one) where the table's metadata is stored

columns.name: zookeeper_path
columns.comment: Path to table data in ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: replica_name
columns.comment: Replica name in ClickHouse Keeper. Different replicas of the same table have different names.

columns.name: replica_path
columns.comment: Path to replica data in ClickHouse Keeper. The same as concatenating 'zookeeper_path/replicas/replica_path'.

columns.name: columns_version
columns.comment: Version number of the table structure. Indicates how many times ALTER was performed. If replicas have different versions, it means some replicas haven't made all of the ALTERs yet.

columns.name: queue_size
columns.comment: Size of the queue for operations waiting to be performed. Operations include inserting blocks of data, merges, and certain other actions. It usually coincides with future_parts.

columns.name: inserts_in_queue
columns.comment: Number of inserts of blocks of data that need to be made. Insertions are usually replicated fairly quickly. If this number is large, it means something is wrong.

columns.name: merges_in_queue
columns.comment: The number of merges waiting to be made. Sometimes merges are lengthy, so this value may be greater than zero for a long time.

columns.name: part_mutations_in_queue
columns.comment: The number of mutations waiting to be made.

columns.name: queue_oldest_time
columns.comment: If `queue_size` greater than 0, shows when the oldest operation was added to the queue.

columns.name: inserts_oldest_time
columns.comment: See `queue_oldest_time`.

columns.name: merges_oldest_time
columns.comment: See `queue_oldest_time`.

columns.name: part_mutations_oldest_time
columns.comment: See `queue_oldest_time`.

columns.name: oldest_part_to_get
columns.comment: The name of the part to fetch from other replicas obtained from the oldest GET_PARTS entry in the replication queue.

columns.name: oldest_part_to_merge_to
columns.comment: The result part name to merge to obtained from the oldest MERGE_PARTS entry in the replication queue.

columns.name: oldest_part_to_mutate_to
columns.comment: The result part name to mutate to obtained from the oldest MUTATE_PARTS entry in the replication queue.

columns.name: log_max_index
columns.comment: Maximum entry number in the log of general activity. This column and the next three (`log_pointer`, `total_replicas`, `active_replicas`) have a non-zero value only where there is an active session with ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: log_pointer
columns.comment: Maximum entry number in the log of general activity that the replica copied to its execution queue, plus one. If log_pointer is much smaller than log_max_index, something is wrong.

columns.name: last_queue_update
columns.comment: When the queue was updated last time.

columns.name: absolute_delay
columns.comment: How big lag in seconds the current replica has.

columns.name: total_replicas
columns.comment: The total number of known replicas of this table.

columns.name: active_replicas
columns.comment: The number of replicas of this table that have a session in ClickHouse Keeper (i.e., the number of functioning replicas).

columns.name: lost_part_count
columns.comment: The number of data parts lost in the table by all replicas in total since table creation. Value is persisted in ClickHouse Keeper and can only increase.

columns.name: last_queue_update_exception
columns.comment: When the queue contains broken entries. Especially important when ClickHouse breaks backward compatibility between versions and log entries written by newer versions aren't parseable by old versions.

columns.name: zookeeper_exception
columns.comment: The last exception message, got if the error happened when fetching the info from ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: replica_is_active
columns.comment: Map between replica name and is replica active.

name: replication_queue
comment: .description Contains information about tasks from replication queues stored in ClickHouse Keeper, or ZooKeeper, for tables in the `ReplicatedMergeTree` family.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Name of the database.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Name of the table.

columns.name: replica_name
columns.comment: Replica name in ClickHouse Keeper. Different replicas of the same table have different names.

columns.name: position
columns.comment: Position of the task in the queue.

columns.name: node_name
columns.comment: Node name in ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Type of the task in the queue, one of: • GET_PART — Get the part from another replica, • ATTACH_PART — Attach the part, possibly from our own replica (if found in the detached folder). You may think of it as a GET_PART with some optimizations as they're nearly identical, • MERGE_PARTS — Merge the parts, • DROP_RANGE — Delete the parts in the specified partition in the specified number range. • …

columns.name: create_time
columns.comment: Date and time when the task was submitted for execution.

columns.name: required_quorum
columns.comment: The number of replicas waiting for the task to complete with confirmation of completion. This column is only relevant for the GET_PARTS task.

columns.name: source_replica
columns.comment: Name of the source replica.

columns.name: new_part_name
columns.comment: Name of the new part.

columns.name: parts_to_merge
columns.comment: Names of parts to merge or update.

columns.name: is_detach
columns.comment: The flag indicates whether the DETACH_PARTS task is in the queue.

columns.name: is_currently_executing
columns.comment: The flag indicates whether a specific task is being performed right now.

columns.name: num_tries
columns.comment: The number of failed attempts to complete the task.

columns.name: last_exception
columns.comment: Text message about the last error that occurred (if any).

columns.name: last_exception_time
columns.comment: Date and time when the last error occurred.

columns.name: last_attempt_time
columns.comment: Date and time when the task was last attempted.

columns.name: num_postponed
columns.comment: The number of times the action was postponed.

columns.name: postpone_reason
columns.comment: The reason why the task was postponed.

columns.name: last_postpone_time
columns.comment: Date and time when the task was last postponed.

columns.name: merge_type
columns.comment: Type of the current merge. Empty if it's a mutation.

name: resources

columns.name: read_disks

name: role_grants

columns.name: role_name

columns.name: granted_role_name

columns.name: granted_role_id
columns.comment: The ID of the role.

columns.name: granted_role_is_default
columns.comment: Flag that shows whether `granted_role` is a default role. Possible values: • 1 — `granted_role` is a default role, • 0 — `granted_role` is not a default role.

columns.name: with_admin_option
columns.comment: Flag that shows whether `granted_role` is a role with `ADMIN OPTION` privilege. Possible values: • 1 — The role has `ADMIN OPTION` privilege. • 0 — The role without `ADMIN OPTION` privilege.

name: row_policies
comment: .description Contains filters for one particular table, as well as a list of roles and/or users which should use this row policy.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of a row policy.

columns.name: short_name
columns.comment: Short name of a row policy. Names of row policies are compound, for example: myfilter ON mydb.mytable. Here 'myfilter ON mydb.mytable' is the name of the row policy, 'myfilter' is it's short name.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Database name.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Table name. Empty if policy for database.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: Row policy ID.

columns.name: storage
columns.comment: Name of the directory where the row policy is stored.

columns.name: select_filter
columns.comment: Expression which is used for filtering in SELECT queries.

columns.name: is_restrictive
columns.comment: Shows whether the row policy restricts access to rows. Value: • 0 — The row policy is defined with `AS PERMISSIVE` clause, • 1 — The row policy is defined with AS RESTRICTIVE clause.

columns.name: apply_to_all
columns.comment: Shows that the row policies set for all roles and/or users.

columns.name: apply_to_list
columns.comment: List of the roles and/or users to which the row policies is applied.

columns.name: apply_to_except
columns.comment: The row policies is applied to all roles and/or users excepting of the listed ones.

name: s3_queue_metadata
comment: .description Contains the current number of processed, processing and failed nodes in keeper for each S3Queue metadata object and, on demand, their contents. Unlike system.s3queue_metadata_cache, which shows the in-memory cache, this table reads the state directly from keeper.

columns.name: zookeeper_path
columns.comment: Path in zookeeper to metadata. For a queue on an auxiliary zookeeper this is the factory key `<zookeeper_name>:<path>`, not the raw keeper path.

columns.name: processed_nodes_count
columns.comment: Number of nodes in the `processed` directory in keeper. Only set for `unordered` mode: in `ordered` mode there are no per-file processed nodes (see `processed_path` instead), so the value is NULL.

columns.name: processing_nodes_count
columns.comment: Number of nodes in the `processing` directory in keeper

columns.name: failed_nodes_count
columns.comment: Number of nodes in the `failed` directory in keeper

columns.name: processed_nodes
columns.comment: Contents (node name -> node data) of the `processed` directory in keeper. Only filled for `unordered` mode. Fetched only when this column is selected.

columns.name: processing_nodes
columns.comment: Contents (node name -> node data) of the `processing` directory in keeper. Fetched only when this column is selected.

columns.name: failed_nodes
columns.comment: Contents (node name -> node data) of the `failed` directory in keeper. Fetched only when this column is selected.

columns.name: processed_path
columns.comment: Last processed path per processed pointer in keeper (relative pointer path -> last processed file path). Only filled for `ordered` mode, where it covers the single, per-bucket and per-partition pointers. Fetched only when this column is selected.

name: s3_queue_settings
comment: .description Contains information about the settings of S3Queue tables. Available from server version `24.10`.

columns.name: database

columns.name: name

comment: .description Contains log entries with information about files processed by the S3Queue engine.

columns.name: hostname

columns.name: clickhouse_version

columns.name: system_processor

columns.name: event_date

columns.comment: Event time of writing this log row

columns.name: uuid

columns.name: processing_start_time
columns.comment: Time of the start of processing the file.

columns.name: processing_end_time
columns.comment: Time of the end of processing the file.

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Exception message if happened.

columns.name: commit_id
columns.comment: Id of the transaction in which this file was committed.

columns.name: commit_time

columns.name: transaction_start_time
columns.comment: Time when the whole processing transaction started.

columns.name: get_object_time_ms

name: s3queue_metadata_cache
comment: .description Contains in-memory state of S3Queue metadata and currently processed rows per file.

columns.name: zookeeper_path
columns.comment: Path in zookeeper to metadata

columns.name: file_path
columns.comment: File path of a file which is being processed

columns.name: file_name
columns.comment: File name of a file which is being processed

columns.name: rows_processed
columns.comment: Currently processed number of rows

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Status of processing: Processed, Processing, Failed, or None for a file which the cache knows but has no state for, e.g. a file whose processing was reset. A non-null `processing_observed_in_keeper_time` means that the `Processing` status was not set by the processor which holds the file, but read from keeper

columns.name: processing_start_time
columns.comment: Time at which processing of the file started

columns.name: processing_end_time
columns.comment: Time at which processing of the file ended

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Exception which happened during processing. Always the one of the last attempt of this server, never the one which keeper stores for the file

columns.name: processing_observed_in_keeper_time
columns.comment: Time at which a processor of this server failed to take the file and read the `Processing` status from keeper instead of setting it itself. Usually the file is held by another server, but it can also be held by a processor of this server which had just taken it. In either case `rows_processed`, `processing_start_time`, `processing_end_time` and `exception` describe the last attempt of this serv…

name: scheduler
comment: .description Contains information about and status of scheduling nodes residing on the local server. This table can be used for monitoring. The table contains a row for every scheduling node.

columns.name: resource
columns.comment: Resource name

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Path to a scheduling node within this resource scheduling hierarchy

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Type of a scheduling node.

columns.name: weight
columns.comment: Weight of a node, used by a parent node of `fair` type.

columns.name: priority
columns.comment: Priority of a node, used by a parent node of 'priority' type (Lower value means higher priority).

columns.name: precedence
columns.comment: Precedence of a node, used by space-shared (memory) parent nodes to order admission and eviction (Lower value means higher precedence).

columns.name: is_active
columns.comment: Whether this node is currently active - has resource requests to be dequeued and constraints satisfied.

columns.name: active_children
columns.comment: The number of children in active state.

columns.name: dequeued_requests
columns.comment: The total number of resource requests dequeued from this node.

columns.name: canceled_requests
columns.comment: The total number of resource requests canceled from this node.

columns.name: rejected_requests
columns.comment: The total number of resource requests rejected from this node.

columns.name: dequeued_cost
columns.comment: The sum of costs (e.g. size in bytes) of all requests dequeued from this node.

columns.name: canceled_cost
columns.comment: The sum of costs (e.g. size in bytes) of all requests canceled from this node.

columns.name: rejected_cost
columns.comment: The sum of costs (e.g. size in bytes) of all requests rejected from this node.

columns.name: busy_periods
columns.comment: The total number of deactivations of this node.

columns.name: throughput
columns.comment: Current average throughput (dequeued cost per second).

columns.name: vruntime
columns.comment: For children of `fair` nodes only. Virtual runtime of a node used by SFQ algorithm to select the next child to process in a max-min fair manner.

columns.name: system_vruntime
columns.comment: For `fair` nodes only. Virtual runtime showing `vruntime` of the last processed resource request. Used during child activation as the new value of `vruntime`.

columns.name: queue_length
columns.comment: For `request_queue` and `allocation_queue` nodes. Current number of resource requests residing in the queue.

columns.name: queue_cost
columns.comment: For `request_queue` and `allocation_queue` nodes. Sum of costs (e.g. size in bytes) of all requests residing in the queue.

columns.name: budget
columns.comment: For `request_queue` nodes. The number of available 'cost units' for new resource requests. Can appear in case of discrepancy of estimated and real costs of resource requests (e.g. after read/write failure)

columns.name: is_satisfied
columns.comment: For constraint nodes only (e.g. `inflight_limit`). Equals to `1` if all the constraint of this node are satisfied.

columns.name: inflight_requests
columns.comment: For `inflight_limit` nodes only. The number of resource requests dequeued from this node, that are currently in consumption state.

columns.name: inflight_cost
columns.comment: For `inflight_limit` nodes only. The sum of costs (e.g. bytes) of all resource requests dequeued from this node, that are currently in consumption state.

columns.name: max_requests
columns.comment: For `inflight_limit` nodes only. Upper limit for inflight_requests leading to constraint violation.

columns.name: max_cost
columns.comment: For `inflight_limit` nodes only. Upper limit for inflight_cost leading to constraint violation.

columns.name: max_speed
columns.comment: For `bandwidth_limit` nodes only. Upper limit for bandwidth in tokens per second.

columns.name: max_burst
columns.comment: For `bandwidth_limit` nodes only. Upper limit for tokens available in token-bucket throttler.

columns.name: throttling_us
columns.comment: For `bandwidth_limit` nodes only. Total number of microseconds this node was in throttling state.

columns.name: tokens
columns.comment: For `bandwidth_limit` nodes only. Number of tokens currently available in token-bucket throttler.

columns.name: allocated
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The currently allocated amount of resource under this node.

columns.name: reclaimable
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. Memory available for new spill requests under this node. For each allocation, outstanding requests are subtracted from its reported reclaimable memory and the result is clamped at zero before summing.

columns.name: reclaiming
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. Memory requested for spilling but not yet settled under this node, including requests that have not started executing. Settlement retires the requested amount independently of the amount actually freed.

columns.name: allocations
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The current number of running resource allocations under this node.

columns.name: updates
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The total number of updates propagated through this node.

columns.name: increases
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The total number of increase requests approved by this node.

columns.name: decreases
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The total number of decrease requests approved by this node.

columns.name: admits
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The total number of allocations admitted by this node.

columns.name: removes
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The total number of allocations removed from this node.

columns.name: killers
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The total number of evictions initiated due to increase requests by this node.

columns.name: victims
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The total number of allocations that were evicted from this node.

columns.name: spills
columns.comment: For space-shared nodes only. The total number of spill requests issued by this node due to its soft memory limit being exceeded.

columns.name: soft_limit
columns.comment: For `allocation_limit` nodes only. The effective soft memory limit above which reclaimable allocations are asked to spill (the smaller of `max_memory_before_spill` and `max_memory_to_spill_ratio * max_memory`). Values not below the hard limit mean spilling is disabled.

columns.name: rejects
columns.comment: For `allocation_queue` nodes only. The total number of resource allocations rejected from this node.

columns.name: pending
columns.comment: For `allocation_queue` nodes only. The current number of pending resource allocations in this node.

name: table_functions

name: tables

columns.name: metadata_modification_time

columns.name: dependencies_database

columns.name: parameterized_view_parameters

columns.name: sorting_key

columns.name: unique_key

columns.name: storage_policy

columns.name: total_rows

columns.name: total_bytes

If the table stores data on disk, returns used space on disk (i.e. compressed). If the table stores data in memory, returns approximated number of used bytes in memory.

columns.name: total_bytes_uncompressed
columns.comment: Total number of uncompressed bytes, if it's possible to quickly determine the exact number of bytes from the part checksums for the table on storage, otherwise NULL (does not take underlying storage (if any) into account).

columns.name: parts
columns.comment: The total number of parts in this table.

columns.name: active_parts
columns.comment: The number of active parts in this table.

columns.name: total_marks
columns.comment: The total number of marks in all parts in this table.

columns.name: active_on_fly_data_mutations
columns.comment: Total number of active data mutations (UPDATEs and DELETEs) suitable for applying on the fly.

columns.name: active_on_fly_alter_mutations
columns.comment: Total number of active alter mutations (MODIFY COLUMN) suitable for applying on the fly.

columns.name: active_on_fly_metadata_mutations
columns.comment: Total number of active metadata mutations (RENAMEs) suitable for applying on the fly.

columns.name: columns_descriptions_cache_size

columns.name: lifetime_rows
columns.comment: Total number of rows INSERTed since server start (only for Buffer tables).

columns.name: lifetime_bytes
columns.comment: Total number of bytes INSERTed since server start (only for Buffer tables).

columns.name: comment

columns.name: has_own_data
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the table itself stores some data on disk or only accesses some other source.

columns.name: loading_dependencies_database

columns.name: loading_dependencies_table

columns.name: loading_dependent_database

columns.name: loading_dependent_table

columns.name: target_database

columns.name: target_table

columns.name: definer

columns.name: clickhouse_version

columns.name: cpu_id
columns.comment: CPU identifier.

columns.name: thread_id
columns.comment: Thread identifier.

columns.name: thread_name
columns.comment: Thread name.

columns.comment: Stack trace at the moment of sampling. On ELF platforms except FreeBSD, addresses inside the main ClickHouse binary are stored as physical file offsets, and frames outside it (shared libraries, JIT code) are stored as 0.

columns.comment: For the memory trace types is a size in bytes: the allocated size for Memory and MemoryAllocatedWithoutCheck; the allocated size, negated on a deallocation, for MemorySample and JemallocSample; the new peak of the tracker for MemoryPeak; the size of the charge to the global memory tracker for MemoryLargeAllocation. For other trace types is 0.

columns.name: ptr
columns.comment: An identifier of the allocated chunk, the same for its allocation and deallocation during one run of the server. It is not the address of the chunk, which is not published.

columns.name: memory_context
columns.comment: Memory Tracker context (only for Memory, MemoryPeak and MemoryLargeAllocation): `Unknown` context is not defined for this trace_type. `Global` represents server context. `User` represents user/merge context. `Process` represents process (i.e. query) context. `Thread` represents thread (thread of particular process) context. `Max` this is a special value means that memory tracker is not blocked …

columns.name: event
columns.comment: For trace type ProfileEvent is the name of updated profile event, for other trace types is an empty string.

columns.name: increment
columns.comment: For trace type ProfileEvent is the amount of increment of profile event, for other trace types is 0.

columns.name: symbols
columns.comment: If the symbolization is enabled, contains demangled symbol names, corresponding to the `trace`. Symbolization can be enabled or disabled in the `symbolize` setting under `trace_log` in the server configuration file; the setting applies to profiler-collected trace types, while rows with the `Instrumentation` trace type are symbolized regardless of it. Symbolization is supported on ELF platforms …

columns.comment: Milliseconds for reading from command stdout.

columns.name: command_write_timeout
columns.comment: Milliseconds for writing to command stdin.

columns.name: pool_size

columns.comment: Whether to send row count before each data chunk (boolean).

columns.comment: Whether to execute command directly (1) or via /bin/bash (0).

columns.name: event_date

columns.name: event_time

For distributed queries read_rows includes the total number of rows read at all replicas. Each replica sends it's read_rows value, and the server-initiator of the query summarizes all received and local values. The cache volumes do not affect this value.

columns.name: read_bytes
columns.comment: Total number of bytes read from all tables and table functions participated in query. It includes usual subqueries, subqueries for IN and JOIN. For distributed queries read_bytes includes the total number of rows read at all replicas. Each replica sends it's read_bytes value, and the server-initiator of the query summarizes all received and local values. The cache volumes do not affect this value.

columns.comment: The number of rows written by the query, including any rows written by downstream inserts triggered by the pipeline, such as attached materialized views. columns.comment: The number of bytes written by the query (uncompressed), including any bytes written by downstream inserts triggered by the pipeline, such as attached materialized views. For a synchronous insert these downstream bytes are recorded on the `query_kind` = `Insert` entry; for an asynchronous insert they are recorded on the `query_kind` = `AsyncInsertFlush` entry, while the client-facing `Insert` e…

columns.comment: Number of rows in the result of a SELECT query, or the number of rows written by an insert. columns.name: memory_usage

columns.name: normalized_query_hash

columns.comment: Type of the query.

columns.name: client_name

columns.name: client_revision

columns.name: client_version_major

columns.name: client_version_minor
columns.comment: Minor version of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.comment: The number of physical joins executed for this query. It is collected from the pipelines as they are built, so it reflects the joins that are left after all optimizations, not the number of JOIN clauses in the query text. A join is counted no matter how deeply it is nested: subqueries, common table expressions, views, views of views and the SELECT of a materialized view triggered by an INSERT a…

columns.name: used_join_algorithms
columns.comment: Algorithms of the joins counted in used_number_of_joins: 'HASH', 'PARALLEL_HASH', 'GRACE_HASH', 'PARTIAL_MERGE', 'FULL_SORTING_MERGE', 'PARALLEL_FULL_SORTING_MERGE', 'IE_JOIN', 'DIRECT', 'PASTE' and 'CONSTANT', sorted and deduplicated, so an algorithm shared by several joins appears once. This is the algorithm that was chosen to execute each join, not the algorithms that the join_algorithm sett…

columns.name: used_join_kinds
columns.comment: Kinds of the joins counted in used_number_of_joins, one element per join, so a kind shared by several joins appears several times. The elements are sorted rather than in execution order. Each kind is the one that was executed, which can differ from the query text, because the optimizer may run a join with its sides swapped and thereby turn LEFT into RIGHT.

columns.name: used_join_strictness
columns.comment: Strictness of the joins counted in used_number_of_joins, one element per join, in the same order as used_join_kinds: the element at a given index describes the same join in both arrays.

columns.name: spilled_to_disk
columns.comment: Operators that wrote data to temporary files on disk (processing in external memory) during query execution, sorted and deduplicated. An empty array means the query ran fully in memory.

columns.name: transaction_id
columns.comment: The identifier of the transaction in scope of which this query was executed.

columns.name: query_cache_usage
columns.comment: Usage of the query cache during query execution. Values: 'Unknown' = Status unknown, 'None' = The query result was neither written into nor read from the query result cache, 'Write' = The query result was written into the query result cache, 'Read' = The query result was read from the query result cache.

columns.name: asynchronous_read_counters
columns.comment: Metrics for asynchronous reading.

columns.name: is_internal
columns.comment: Indicates whether it is an auxiliary query executed internally.

name: users
comment: .description Contains a list of user accounts configured on the server.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: User name.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: User ID.

columns.name: storage
columns.comment: Path to the storage of users. Configured in the access_control_path parameter.

columns.name: auth_type
columns.comment: Shows the authentication types. There are multiple ways of user identification: with no password, with plain text password, with SHA256-encoded password, with double SHA-1-encoded password or with bcrypt-encoded password.

columns.name: auth_params
columns.comment: Authentication parameters in the JSON format depending on the auth_type.

columns.name: valid_until
columns.comment: The expiration date and time for user credentials, one per authentication method. The stored value is an absolute instant rendered in the server or session time zone; the stored value `0` (the Unix epoch, rendered as `1970-01-01 00:00:00` on a server in `UTC`) is the sentinel meaning the credentials never expire.

columns.name: auth_grants
columns.comment: For each authentication method: the limit of the access rights specified in the `GRANTS` clause, or an empty string if the access rights are not limited.

columns.name: host_ip
columns.comment: IP addresses of hosts that are allowed to connect to the ClickHouse server.

columns.name: host_names
columns.comment: Names of hosts that are allowed to connect to the ClickHouse server.

columns.name: host_names_regexp
columns.comment: Regular expression for host names that are allowed to connect to the ClickHouse server.

columns.name: host_names_like
columns.comment: Names of hosts that are allowed to connect to the ClickHouse server, set using the LIKE predicate.

columns.name: default_roles_all
columns.comment: Shows that all granted roles set for user by default.

columns.name: default_roles_list
columns.comment: List of granted roles provided by default.

columns.name: default_roles_except
columns.comment: All the granted roles set as default excepting of the listed ones.

columns.name: grantees_any
columns.comment: The flag that indicates whether a user with any grant option can grant it to anyone.

columns.name: grantees_list
columns.comment: The list of users or roles to which this user is allowed to grant options to.

columns.name: grantees_except
columns.comment: The list of users or roles to which this user is forbidden from grant options to.

columns.name: default_database
columns.comment: The name of the default database for this user.

name: view_refreshes
comment: .description Information about Refreshable Materialized Views. Contains all refreshable materialized views, regardless of whether there's a refresh in progress or not.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: The name of the database the table is in.

columns.name: view
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: uuid
columns.comment: Table uuid (Atomic database).

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Current state of the refresh.

columns.name: last_success_time
columns.comment: Time when the latest successful refresh started. NULL if no successful refreshes happened since server startup or table creation.

columns.name: last_success_duration_ms
columns.comment: How long the latest refresh took.

columns.name: last_refresh_time
columns.comment: Time when the latest refresh attempt finished (if known) or started (if unknown or still running). NULL if no refresh attempts happened since server startup or table creation.

columns.name: last_refresh_replica
columns.comment: If coordination is enabled, name of the replica that made the current (if running) or previous (if not running) refresh attempt.

columns.name: next_refresh_time
columns.comment: Time at which the next refresh is scheduled to start on this replica (unless another replica starts it first). NULL if the next refresh time is not currently known, e.g. when waiting for dependencies (status `WaitingForDependencies` or `MissingDependencies`).

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Error message from previous attempt if it failed.

columns.name: retry
columns.comment: How many failed attempts there were so far, for the current refresh. Not available if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`.

columns.name: progress
columns.comment: Progress of the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica, between 0 and 1. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica` or the refresh is not running.

columns.name: read_rows
columns.comment: Number of rows read by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`.

columns.name: read_bytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`

columns.name: total_rows
columns.comment: Estimated total number of rows that need to be read by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`

columns.name: written_rows
columns.comment: Number of rows written by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`

columns.name: written_bytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes written by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`

name: warnings
comment: .description This table shows warnings about the ClickHouse server. Warnings of the same type are combined into a single warning. For example, if the number N of attached databases exceeds a configurable threshold T, a single entry containing the current value N is shown instead of N separate entries. If current value drops below the threshold, the entry is removed from the table.

columns.name: message
columns.comment: A warning message issued by ClickHouse server.

columns.name: message_format_string
columns.comment: A format string that was used to format the message.

name: workloads
comment: .description Contains information for workloads residing on the local server. The table contains a row for every workload.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The name of the workload.

columns.name: parent
columns.comment: The name of the parent workload.

columns.name: create_query
columns.comment: CREATE query of the workload.

name: zeros
comment: .description Produces unlimited number of non-materialized zeros.

columns.name: zero
columns.comment: dummy

name: zeros_mt
comment: .description Multithreaded version of system.zeros.

columns.name: zero
columns.comment: dummy

name: zookeeper_connection_log
comment: .description The 'system.zookeeper_connection_log' table shows the history of ZooKeeper connections (including auxiliary ZooKeepers). Each row shows information about one event regarding connections.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server which is connected to or disconnected from ZooKeeper.

columns.name: clickhouse_version
columns.comment: Version of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: system_processor
columns.comment: CPU architecture of the ClickHouse server that produced the row.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: The type of the event. Possible values: Connected, Disconnected.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Date of the entry.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Time of the entry

columns.name: event_time_microseconds
columns.comment: Time of the entry with microseconds precision.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: ZooKeeper cluster's name.

columns.name: host
columns.comment: The hostname/IP of the ZooKeeper node that ClickHouse connected to or disconnected from.

columns.name: port
columns.comment: The port of the ZooKeeper node that ClickHouse connected to or disconnected from.

columns.name: index
columns.comment: The index of the ZooKeeper node that ClickHouse connected to or disconnected from. The index is from ZooKeeper config.

columns.name: client_id
columns.comment: Session id of the connection.

columns.name: keeper_api_version
columns.comment: Keeper API version.

columns.name: enabled_feature_flags
columns.comment: Feature flags which are enabled. Only applicable to ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: availability_zone
columns.comment: Availability zone

columns.name: reason
columns.comment: Reason for the connection or disconnection.
